tender.description: Europe has built world leading Earth Observation (EO) infrastructures, but today's exploitation paradigm remains fragmented and focused on data pipelines rather than integrated intelligence. As a result, transforming EO data into actionable insights is slow, difficult to scale, and poorly aligned with the needs of non space industries. Meanwhile, global digital leaders are advancing rapidly with geospatial foundation models, world models and agentic AI systems that reason across heterogeneous data. Without a comparable European capability, much of the value generated from European EO assets risks being externalised.To address this, the proposed activity aims to prototype a World Agentic Engine (WAE), an agentic, AI driven capability able to orchestrate models, data, and servicesusing a shared semantic layer. Built around multi mission geospatial embeddings, GFMs, and world models, it will support reasoning,prediction, scenario exploration, and cross domain decision making. Rather than duplicating data, the WAE will interface with existing infrastructures and integrate both institutional and commercial actors. A key objective is to develop and to validate the economic model of the World Agentic Engine, which will federate institutional and commercial players within a European-centric ecosystem. The system will use a usage-based transaction economical model, where each information/action/knowledge unit invocation is recorded and feeds a revenue-sharing scheme among unit owners, service operators, compute and data providers, including commercial and restricted datasets (e.g., national constellations), while taking in account the individual national data policies.By doing so, the World Agentic Engine will strengthen Europe's positioning in the Earth Intelligence domain, moving out from a plethora of isolated EO applications and services towards an integrated and open ecosystem for Earth Intelligence, based on European data, capable of supporting scientific discovery, commercial services, enabling policy monitoring and validation in a coherent and scalable manner, able tocapture the collective value of European's investments.The activity will demonstrate technical feasibility and economic viabilitythrough five development pillars: agentic orchestration, system integration, multi model support, commercialisation strategy, and pilot use cases. A primary pilot will support FAO and national forest monitoring systems, showcasing AI driven reporting and climate finance applications. Additional pilots will explore domains where agentic EO intelligence delivers operational impact. By doing so,the WAE aims to demonstrate Earth Intelligence, moving from isolated applications to an integrated, scalable, sovereign European ecosystem.

Recent demonstrations of Avalanche Photodiode (APD) technology in MCT layers opens up the possibility of signal magnification at the pixel level which reduces the effective readout noise. This can unlock performance improvements through an enhanced Signal-to-Noise ratio (SNR),or allow operation at equivalent SNR but with faster frame rates (reducing ground sampling distances, or allowing higher operating temperatures). Prototype APD structures in MCT material shall be designed and manufactured, and coupled to a high performance readout circuit suited for Earth Observation applications. Detailed electro-optic characterisation shall be performed, to compare to equivalent detectors manufactured with a standard MCT technology. The advantage/disadvantages of the technology shall be assessed for a range of EO applications. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Expected performance simulation for an Earth Observation ROIC operated with an APD detection layer - Design and manufacture of test samples with APD designs - Characterisation of device performance - Critical assessment of test results, including comparison to performance simulation and design expectations.

tender.description: Objective: To develop a E-/W-band traveling wave tube slow-wave structure breadboard capable of delivering 100 W of output power.Description: The millimetre wave domain is also known as the extremely high-frequency (EHF) spectrum ranges from 30 to 300 GHz. Early works on atmospheric propagation in EHF evidenced encouraging future usage for satellite communications. The allocated W-band for satellite services (71-76 GHz and 81-86 GHz) potentially provides a favourable attenuation window due to low oxygen absorption. The exploitation of W-band may offer broad bandwidths for high data rate information transfer. Hence the development of the high power amplifiers is a critical building block that acts as an enabler to exploit this frequency band for satellite telecommunications. Currently, solid state power amplifiers cover this frequency band, but with output powers significantly lower than 100 W and very low efficiency. A traveling wave tube amplifier (TWTA) solution offers better performance in terms of output power and efficiency. This activity aims at developing a traveling wave tube slow-wave structure in W-band, capable of delivering 100 W of output power. As a result of the validation of this key building block, European industry will gain crucial knowledge and pass a first important milestoneon their way to design and manufacture full TWTs in this frequency band. At present, no W-band space TWTs are available in Europe. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Design a traveling wave tube slow-wave structure in W-band, capable of delivering 100 W of output power - Manufacturing of a breadboard - Testing and validation of a breadboardDeliverables: Breadboard, Report

tender.description: Objective: To develop low barrier Schottky diodes and mixers for passive remote sensing of the Earth's atmosphere, with a local oscillator power requirement less than 25% compared to a traditional GaAs mixer.Description: Traditional Gallium Arsenide mixers such as the one used for MetOp-SG Micro Wave Imager (MWI) and Micro Wave Sounder (MWS) and Ice Cloud Imager (ICI) instruments need few milliwatts of local oscillator (LO) power to reach optimal conversion efficiency and noise figure. For single pixel instruments, this is well achievable with current local oscillator technology. For extended arrays of heterodyne receivers, this would mean to increase the local oscillator power requirements by one or two orders of magnitude. Therefore, the need for low LO power mixers is key to develop extended arrays of heterodyne receivers. This can be achieved by implementing a direct current (DC) biasing circuit together with GaAs mixer technology. This increases the complexity of the mixer circuit. An alternative solution is to implement low-barrier mixers using alternative semiconductor technology to reduce the barrier-height of the Schottky contact and similarly the pump power level, without the need for external DC biasing. The objective of this activity is to develop low-barrier diodes and mixers at EarthObservation applicable frequencies in the millimetre-wave and sub-THz regions of the spectrum. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Review of the current state-of-the-art in terms of low-barrier Schottky technology available (InGaAs, SiGe,...). - Design, manufacture and test a low-barrier diode and mixer operating in the 166-664 GHz range - Perform analysis of the performance, lessons learned and propose roadmap for future developments.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. tender.description: Objective: To develop a breadboard of a distributed temperature sensor using a fibre optic to measure the temperature of large deployable reflectors.Description: Missions such as CIMR which use a Large Deployable Reflectors (LDR) for radiometry require knowledge of the reflector temperature during observation in order to increase the accuracy of the measurement. This is a very challenging temperature measurement, both on orbit and on-ground, due to the very thin wires of the mesh structure, together with the gold coating of the wires. Contact thermometers, infra-red thermography and electrical techniques have all been proposed, each coming with their own set of challenges. The use of a fibre optic Distributed Temperature Sensor (DTS) is an alternative approach to infer LDR temperature both on-ground and in-orbit. The use of a gold-plated fibre - which matches the thermo-optical properties of the mesh wires -allows the fibre to act as a temperature measurement proxy for the LDR itself. In addition, the DTS allows temperature to be read out continuously along the fibre over a long distance (e.g. very 2.5cm over tens of metres) from a single interrogator. The use of Raman scattering DTS with a gold coated fibre has already been proposed for the CIMR-like use case with basic feasibility demonstrated. The activity aims to test and characterize at a representative scale this measurement method and build a breadboard which can be developed for future EO mission. The use of a fibre optic does raise a number of practical challenges, for example the safe handling of the fibre during AIT, and the integration with a deployable structure for flight application. The activity will therefore assess the practical feasibility of the technique in a realistic industrial setting. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Requirements consolidation and assessment of state of the art - Design of breadboard and associated test bench - Manufacture of breadboard, test bench - Execution of tests and exploitation of results - Roadmap for further development towards a flight applicationDeliverables: Breadboard, Report, Software

tender.description: ARCH-AI addresses the rapid transition of numerical weather prediction (NWP), ocean prediction (NOP), and climate forecasting toward AI/ML-driven approaches. These methods enable faster forecasts, larger ensembles, and new probabilistic capabilities, but they fundamentally change what is required from Earth Observation.The key shift is from EO as an observational system to EO as an integralcomponent of predictive systems. This means observations are no longer just inputs; they must be optimised for AI training, inference, and continuous model evolution.Current European EO systems are strong but not designed for this paradigm. The ARCH-AI studies examines how the entire EO system-of-systems (space, ground, data, interfaces) must evolve to support AI-native and hybrid forecasting,while maintaining continuity, reliability, and European strategic autonomy.The ARCH-AI studies will deliver a set of coherent Earth Observation architecture options (3-5), spanning AI-native, hybrid, and observation-centric designs, each characterised in terms of performance, cost, risk, and dependencies. These are grounded in a reformulation of EO requirements derived directly from AI/ML needs, including data characteristics for training and inference, and trade-offs between temporal sampling, resolution, and long-termstability.The studies will define transition pathways from current systems, and translate architectures into programme and investment scenarios, including mission portfolios and options for maintaining European strategic autonomy. The study outputs will be used tohelp align future EO investments with AI-driven forecasting needs, ensuring that Europe's EO system evolves into an integrated, AI-ready prediction infrastructure that remains operationally relevant and competitive.

tender.description: To derive more accurate expression of atmosphere irregularities effects with a focus on the ionosphere, and devise mitigation techniques for both geo- and sun-synchronous SAR imaging systemsDescription: For Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) systems the atmospheric turbulence is generally assumed to be time-invariant during the synthetic aperture time due to itsshort duration. Such assumption is not always correct, as horizontal atmospheric drifts and vortices exist. Especially for SAR systems at low frequency (P-Band, L-Band), SAR operating on repeat-track basis, geo-synchronous SAR systems characterised by long integration time and extensive imaging scene, the ionosphere can have an important role on the performance. Furthermore, both temporal andspatial variations of the ionosphere have to be jointly taken into account, which further complicates their characterisation. Therefore, the effects of the flowing ionospheric irregularities need to be investigated, aiming in particular to image shifts, defocusing and repeat-track interferometry. The aim of this activity is to provide a comprehensive analysis to evaluate effects of both spatial variation and flowing ionospheric irregularities on SAR systems operating both at P-, L- and C-band. In particular, the ionospheric scintillations, which act remarkably in the polar cap and equatorial zone at night need to be considered. The Ionosphere characterisation shall originate from previous developments, analyses performed in the framework of previous missions developments and from knowledge built up in the navigation community. This activity encompasses the following tasks: -Analytical models of the physical effects of spatial-temporally ionospheric background variations on the SAR signal. - Assessment of the impacts on the SAR performancesdemonstrating, both theoretically and numerically, the geometric fidelity, focusing aspect and interferometry quality (i.e., relative image shifts and the decorrelation of interferometric pairs, interferometric phase screen errors). - Validation of the models andof the performance analysis using ionospheric monitoring measurements (i.e., Global Positioning System). - Develop mitigation techniques. - The implementation of the aforementioned components in a software framework. The methods developed in this activity are expected to be developed in such a way that they can be later broadened to other atmospheric effects such as tropospheric scintillations. Software shall be delivered under an ESA Software Community License, so that any individuals or entities within ESA Member Statescan access to it and can provide update to the community of users.Deliverables: Report, SoftwareProcurement Policy: C(3) = Activity restricted to SMEs  RD  Entities. tender.description: The objective of this activity is to develop a physically-based framework that describes and simulates the temporal variation and fluctuations of the scattered SAR signal induced by vegetation. To achieve this, the Contractor shall define such framework and its architecture, along with the necessary interfaces, the different components, and the expected inputs and outputs, focusing on representing the scattering of SAR signals by vegetated land surfaces. The framework shall be modular and applicable to a wide range of present and future missions and scenarios, and shall allow the use and intercomparison of different modelling approaches. It shall be designed to:1.           cover multiple frequencies of the incident signal, with a focus on C-band and L-band as a minimum2.    accommodate the simulations of the effects of several categories of vegetation, e.g. from forests to agricultural fields3.      capture different temporal scales of the signal evolution in the simulations, that could range for example from seconds to days4.           Output the complex scattered field, which can then be used for subsequent performance analysisFurther, the Contractor shall develop the models that go into the framework and validate them using existing spaceborne, airborne and on-ground datasetswhen available. The models shall be physically-based, describe the scattering mechanisms with sufficient accuracy, and shall be parameterized and validated using experimental observations. The validation shall be focused on a limited number of scenarios, that must be representative of candidate SAR missions (like Hydroterra+) and planned SAR missions (e.g. ROSE-L). After implementation and validation, the Contractor shall analyse the outputs of the simulations and conduct sensitivity analyses, to understand and characterize the impact of vegetation on both amplitude and phase of the output observations, and its effect on the Single Look Complex (SLC) and interferometric products.
tender.title: A PHYSICALLY-BASED MULTI-TIMESCALE MODELLING FRAMEWORK OF DYNAMIC VEGETATION SIGNALS FOR SAR - EXPRO PLUS

tender.description: Activity 2B addresses Phase B of the Alpstar Federation Layer, aiming to consolidate requirements, architecture, and prototype validation for a federated, multi stakeholder space system. Building on the MRD 2.0, this phase will define and specify all functional, technical, and security requirements of the Federation Layer, including secure interfaces with commercial service providers and Alpstar Nodes via unidirectional "diode" connections.The activity encompasses the full design of the Alpstar system architecture and the development and demonstration of a User Ground Segment prototype. Comprehensive specifications will be produced for all major Federation Layer components, ensuring interoperability, security, and scalability across federated participants.The procurement also includes the acquisition of a minimum of three months of satellite data, necessary to support validation and testing of the Ground Segment prototype under operationally representative conditions.A key deliverable of this phase is a User Ground Segment prototype featuring:A role based user interface, enabling differentiated access and operational views.An initial implementation of the Digital Governance Agent (DGA), enforcing a first set of provisional federation rules and acting as the central mission management and planning capability.The Alpstar Federated Layer shall integrate the following core functionalities:Digital Governance Agent (DGA)for federation rule enforcement and central mission managementSecure Data Pooling Service for controlled dissemination of observation resultsFederated Ledger to record and audit transactionsStandardised APIs interfacing with Nodes (FOS and PDGS)Federated Data Lake hosted in a cloud environmentVirtual Constellation Management for coordinated asset utilisationFederated CatalogueCross federation taskingNATO FMN / Joint ISR tasking interfaces routed to AlpstarRole based user interfaceFederation dashboard for operational and governance oversightWith a target duration of 12 months, the expected outcomes of Activity 2B include:Complete specifications of the Federation LayerDefinition of the Federation Layer architectureRough Order of Magnitude (ROM)cost estimate for implementationIdentification of the industrial consortiumDevelopment plan and integrated scheduleDemonstration of the User Ground Segment prototypeThis phase will provide the technical, architectural, and organisational foundations required to progress Alpstar toward a fully operational, secure, and governed federated space capability.
tender.title: ERS-EO ALPSTAR FEDERATED LAYER DEFINITION AND PRELIMINARY IMPLEMENTATION (ACTIVITY 2B)

tender.description: The ALPSTAR Phase A/B1 study for a bespoke X band SAR mission, with optional ELINT capability, aims to define a technically feasible, sovereign European space segment architecture aligned with emerging user needs and the ALPSTAR federated concept. Conducted through up to two parallel industrial contracts within participating states, the study focuses on the design of a high performance SAR payload as the primary driver, including its integration on a mature platform (TRL 8-9), while assessing the feasibility, added value,and implementation impacts of incorporating an ELINT capability either as an embedded or hosted payload. The activity includes mission and system architecture definition, interface specification with the ground and federation layers, compliance with SRD and evolving MRD use cases, and evaluation of key technologies and TRL gaps. It further delivers preliminary design solutions, end to end performance considerations (including L0/L1 processing and ELINT simulation), trade offs, and a credible roadmap toward flight readiness. Outputs also encompass a comprehensive development and procurement plan, industrial organisation, launcher options, and robust ROMcost and schedule estimates for subsequent B2/C/D/E phases, ensuring decision readiness for the ALPSTAR Governance Board.
tender.title: ERS-EO ALPSTAR PHASE A/B1 STUDY FOR A BESPOKE SAR MISSION WITH OPTIONAL ELINT (ACTIVITY 3)

tender.description: EGV Pilot is an ESA pilot study aimed at structuring, mapping and assessing the geodetic foundations required to support future Earth Observation missions and Earth system science. The activity focuses on the role of geodetic observations and products as foundational enablers for Earth system monitoring, mission preparation, and the generation of long term geodetic data records. It builds on internationally coordinated developments on Essential Geodetic Variables (EGVs), in particular within GGOS and IAG, and translates these advances into an ESA-relevant framework aligned with the Earth Observation Science Strategy (EOSS), FutureEO missions, and other ESA programmatic elements. The study will establish clear traceability between geodetic requirements, products, observing systems and future EO missions. It will assess the readiness and maturity of geodetic observations and products, identify missing or degraded capabilities, and analyse how future ESA space and ground segment infrastructures could strengthen the geodetic foundations. Explicit consideration will be given to synergies with ESA missions such as GENESIS and NGGM/MAGIC, as well as to preparedness for integration into Digital Twin Earth.
tender.title: EGV-PILOT: GEODETIC FOUNDATIONS FOR FUTURE EARTH OBSERVATION - EXPRO PLUS

tender.description: To develop, manufacture and test low loss high power (>37 dBm peak) acoustic wave filters for UHF, L- and S-band applications.Description: Acoustic Wave filters offer a drastically reduced size and weight compared to other filter technologies, such ascavity and planar filters, and are often employed in payload receivers and frequency converters. However, standard acoustic filter technology suffers from poor power handling capability, which prevents its use at the output section of telecommunication payloads. Various technical advances are ongoing in the frame of 5G terrestrial infrastructure applications to overcome the power limitation. Recent developments in advanced engineered substrates such guided surface acoustic wave (SAW) and single crystal bulk acoustic wave (XBAW), openthe possibility of developing high performance and medium filter components. Recently, up to 40-Watt peak power filterscentered at 3.55 GHz have been demonstrated. The technology could also offer semiconductor compatibility, enabling high integrationof RF front ends. This activity will assess several techniques to improve the power handling of acoustic wave based filters for on-board space applications, including reducing circuit losses, accelerating heat dissipation, and enhancing the resistance of acoustomigration and electro-migration. This activity aims at developing miniature high power acoustic wave filter technology for UHF, L- and S-band to support the realization of wavelength agnostic space telecommunication payloads. The availability of high power acousticfilters will enable higher integration and miniaturization of payloads output section. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Requirements consolidation. - Trade-off analysis and identification of the most promising technology candidates. - Preliminary design and critical prototyping of acoustic resonators to de-risk the design. - Detailed design and analysis of filter breadboards. - Manufacturingand integration. - Testing and validation in relevant environment including power handling tests.
tender.title: HIGH POWER ACOUSTIC FILTERS - EXPRO PLUS

tender.description: This activity focuses on designing and optimizing Position, Velocity, and Time (PVT) engines specifically for LEO-based PNT systems. It aims to exploit the unique measurement diversity offered by LEO satellites, such as multipath whitening, Doppler utilization, and rapid LOS/NLOS transitions. Two approaches will be developed and compared: a conventional Kalman filter-based design and an AI/ML-based design to handle unexpected LEO measurement behaviours. The study will include state-of-the-art review, algorithm development, and benchmarking against traditional MEO GNSS-based engines. Field measurement campaigns will validate performance and inform a roadmap for commercialization. For more info, visit https://navisp.esa.int/opportunity
tender.title: NAVISP-EL1-124-OPTIMISATION OF PVT ENGINES FOR LEO MEASUREMENT DIVERSITY - EXPRO+

tender.description: Objective: To develop a complete Software product portfolio of building blocks facilitating the integration of ADHA platforms in Mid-size LEO satellite platforms.Description: The Advanced Data Handling Architecture (ADHA) has been developed as a set of hardware components with standardized communication interfaces. Previous work has focused on the hardware aspects, but the current situation highlights the need for a robust software stack to support ADHA in space missions, in particular mid-sized LEO satellites. The main concern is to ensure that enough software components are ready for use in flight and developed using modern, modular techniques to enhance compatibility and performance. This activity aims to provide a modular software stack that can be utilized across different ADHA-based computers, including On-Board Computers (OBCs) and Instrument Control Units (ICUs) from various vendors. By leveraging different European processors, FPGA, and other COTS processors commonly used in commercial satellites, the software stack is aimed at offering flexibility and interoperability. The added value includes improved mission reliability, reduced development time, and cost savings through standardized software components. The configuration and deployment of the software will be integrated into a model-based software development and code generation tools such as TASTE using Space Creator, facilitating streamlined development and deployment processes. Future activities may involve further refinement of the software stack, extending compatibility to additional processors, and continuous improvement based on user feedback and mission requirements. This activity encompasses the following tasks: -Assessing the feasibility of a modular software stack for different ADHA-based computers. - Developing the software stack to support multiple European processors. - Integrating the software stack into a software MBSE toolset (e.g. TASTE). - Testing and validatingthe software stack across different hardware configurations. - Documenting the development process and results. Software shall be delivered under an ESA Software Community Licence, allowing access and updates by individuals or entities within ESA Member States.
tender.title: ADHA SOFTWARE ARCHITECTURE - EXPRO+

tender.description: Objective: To evaluate options standardisation around Ethernet, including connectors and software protocols - and to identify enablers for utilisation of Ethernet in mid-size satellites.Description: Mid- and small-size satellite providers increasingly rely on COTS technologies to meet stringent market cost requirements. The use of COTS FPGAs has enabled space-specific command, control, and data interfaces, while COTS processors are increasingly adopted in data handling equipment. These processors typically provide terrestrial electrical interfaces such as Ethernet. Interest in Ethernet for on-board data handling is growing, driven by the availability of new devices and the ability of later Ethernet versions to support very high data rates (up to 100 Gbit/s). Ethernet up to 100 Mbps has already been used successfully in ESA programmes, including human spaceflight, and several initiatives have explored its usein critical applications. However, Ethernet adoption in space raises new challenges: -No standardised or widely accepted flight connector exists for Ethernet (1GbE, 10GbE and above). -Ethernet introduces additional layers in the protocol stack (e.g., UDP/TCP at the transport layer and IP at the network layer). Further work is needed to determine how best to implement and optimise application-layer protocols on top of these. -Many data handling system elements (e.g., payload front-ends) rely on FPGAs, and integrating Ethernet IPs requires additional considerations. This activity addresses the technology gap for end-to-end interoperable 1GbE and higher Ethernet in mid-size satellites and identify elements for standardisation to enhance equipment reusability and strengthen European competitiveness. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Assess Ethernet flight connector options for 1GbE, 10GbE, and higher rates, considering ESA mission heritage and available connectors. - Assess suitable software application protocols for use with Ethernet and standard stacks, ensuring implementation feasibility in FPGAs, qualified RTOS, and Linux. -Study the availability of EEE components implementing Ethernet building blocks (processors, transceivers, switches, etc.) and derive a roadmap for adoption. -Manufacture, test, and validate Ethernet implementations across different microelectronics options (e.g., processors, FPGAs), identifying performance, integration, and qualification considerations. - Deliver a breadboard setup implementing selected flight connector candidates, software protocols, and EEE/microelectronics components identified above Software shall be delivered under an ESA SoftwareCommunity Licence, so that any individuals or entities within ESA Member States can access it and can provide update to the community of users.Deliverables: Breadboard, Report
tender.title: ETHERNET CONNECTIVITY FOR MID-SIZE SATELLITES EXPRO PLUS

tender.description: Objective:To develop and optimise additive manufacturing techniques for ceramic components, as well as developing post-processing,improving crack detection and establishing a robust European supply chain.Description:Ceramics play a crucial role in spacecraftfor their unique properties, namely high thermal stability/resistance, low density and high strength. Ceramics like silicon carbide(SiC) and silicon nitride (Si3N4) are employed in structural components, delivering high stiffness with relatively low mass. They are vital for optical applications for a stable and accurate placement of sensors and mirrors. They are also used for thermal protectionsystems, microwave and radio-frequency equipment. Recently, additive manufacturing (AM) has further expanded the applications ofceramics in spacecraft, enabling the production of unprecedented complex shapes. Overall, ceramics are becoming indispensable for modern spacecraft.Nevertheless, ESA recognises the need to enhance several key aspects of the ceramic manufacturing chainto supportindustrialisation and establish a robust supply. Despite the advancements in AM, specific challengespersist, particularly when attempting to achieve thin walls, improving surface finish or enabling more intricatelattice geometries with high reliability and precision. The feasibility of assembling larger structures from smallerceramic parts is a way to overcome AM equipment size and processlimitations. In parallel, there is a need toimprove data for crack analysis and damage tolerance, coupled with the development of viableNon-Destructive Testing (NDT) solutions for crack detection. Downstream operations are critical, including precisionmachining formounting interfaces, coatings and polishing. Additionally, exploration of alternatives to SiC and Si3N4 may yield new opportunities. The use of ceramics poses challenges for spacecraft demisability, which can limit their suitability for satellites in large constellations adhering to the zero-debris charter. This constraint must be considered early in the design phase and accounted for in mission architecture.The aim of this activity is to further develop AM processes for ceramics. It can be expected that this will involve the use of novel materials, achieving higher geometric complexity, improved surface finish, larger part size and/or thinner walls.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Trade-off potential use cases (e.g. parts, AM processes and materials) whichwould allow further developingceramic manufacturing technologies for space applications.- Select the most promising application and develop the corresponding AM processes, progressing towards arepresentative part prototype. This will likely involve complementary steps such as surface treatments, joining, coating, polishing and NDT.- Develop numerical simulation tools to support design formanufacturing, for example by predictingdeformation and crack formation during fabrication or sintering.- Manufacture and test the prototype under relevant conditions.- Define end-of-life strategies.Deliverables: Breadboard, Prototype part, Report
tender.title: INNOVATIVE CERAMIC MANUFACTURING FOR SPACE APPLICATIONS - EXPRO+

tender.description: IMPACT 10 is an ESA Earth Observation activity aimed at assessing and demonstrating the scientific and socio economic value generated by selected activities of the Earth and Mission Science Division (EOP SM). It focuses on scientific studies, mission science contributions, and programme enabling work supporting future EO missions. It also covers a new branch of "Future Science" activities. Within EOP SM, "Future Science" refers to forward looking science studies aligned with the ESA EO Science Strategy. These studies are designed to address fundamental Earth system science gaps that are not covered by current or planned missions. They therefore go beyond the scope of existing Science Plans activities. The activity will develop a robust and traceable methodology to assess both science impact and socio economic impact. Science impact will include, for example, scientific outputs, modelling advances, retrieval improvements, uncertainty characterisation, mission requirement support, community building, and uptake in international assessments. Socio economic impact will include, for example, industrial competitiveness, innovation spillovers, policy support, and broader societal and economic value.
tender.title: IMPACT-10: SCIENTIFIC AND SOCIO-ECONOMIC IMPACT ASSESSMENT OF EARLY EARTH OBSERVATION SCIENCE ACTIVITIES- EXPRO PLUS

tender.description: This activity aims to prepare a future in-orbit demonstrator of novel Positioning, Navigation and Timing (PNT) concepts based on quantum technologies. The study will investigate the integration of quantum inertial sensors, advanced timing techniques, including optical clocks, and hybrid navigation architectures combining quantum and classical sensors.Emphasis will be placed on system resilience, autonomy and GNSS-independent navigation including applications in Earth orbit and beyond. The activity will include system-level definition, performance assessment and critical pre-developments, including sensor fusion and onboard processing techniques.The objective is to mature concepts and associated key technologies up to TRL 5/6 and deliver a credible mission concept for a future PNT demonstrator.
tender.title: QUANTUM-ENABLED PNT DEMONSTRATOR PHASES 0/A/B1

tender.description: Objective:The objective of this study is to assess the feasibility of applying Common Criteria framework (or equivalent) to guarantee compatible security mechanisms with HydRON (High-throughput Optical Network).Targeted Improvements:To achieve security interoperability of HydRON with other networks with a clear protection profile definition in line with international standards.Description:Multiple constellations are expected to be developed in the coming years, addressing different applications, like navigation, Earth Observation and communications as well as defence. Each constellation will be optimized for the target application, in terms of technologies, coverage, but also security functions. The challenge, but also the opportunity is to make use of all the possible infrastructure to enhance coverage and resilience of these systems by the integration of optical communication security features like Low Probability to be detected or interfered (LPD/LPI).However, different users will have different protection profiles and thereforesecurity targets will differ between networks. The Common Criteria for Information Technology Security Evaluation (referred to as Common Criteria) is an international standard (ISO/IEC 15408) used to specify security functional and assurance requirements, to guarantee implementation and verification of the security features and it can be used as a baseline for the security analysis of different networks and interoperability of security levels.This activity shall define a set of protection profiles for different target users and identify the security targets for different networks. Taking HydRON as a baseline for communications, the activity shall consider additional, selected national or EC networks interconnected by optical links in space or with optical ground stations and ground networks.For such security interoperability, the activity will define the required security functions (confidentiality, integrity, availability, authentication, non-repudiation...) and achievable levels of assurance by the different space networks. For the sected networks, an analysis of the impact shall be performed for each of these security functions, including a preliminary assessment of vulnerabilities by different potential threat actors and its impact on the system. The feasibility of applying Common Criterialframework or similar framework for these networks shall be assessed. Additionally, the achievable level of protection by the different networks shall be provided as a draft catalogue, to be presented to potential users. The activity shall define initial access scenarios for Ministries of Defence (MODs) and Civil Security Entities to utilise the upcoming HydRON installation to conduct dedicated, potentially classified testingvalidating defencegrade security, resilience behaviours, and interoperability in realistic operational scenarios and providing inputs to preliminary vulnerability assessment analysing operational impacts of potential attacks.
tender.title: HYDRON RESILIENCE: SECURITY ASPECTS OF NETWORKS INTEROPERABILITY (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 3A.240) EXPRO+

tender.description: This activity addresses the evolution of small satellite platforms toward sustainable space operations, in line with ESA's Zero Debris objectives and Ecodesign policy. It aims to consolidate system-level requirements for the next generation small satellite platform, integrating space debris mitigation constraints and environmental sustainability considerations across the full life cycle. Building on previous ESA and industry studies, the activity will identify key design drivers, perform trade-offs, and define a baseline platform concept up to System Requirements Review (SRR) level. It will also assess enabling technologies, engage with European suppliers, and establish a roadmap toward platform maturation and future demonstration. In parallel, the activity will analyse mission scenarios, hosted payload opportunities, and commercialisation aspects to support the preparation of a potential In-Orbit Demonstration (IOD). Overall, the objective is to support the development of reusable satellite product lines that embed Zero Debris compliance and Ecodesign principles while maintaining technical and economic viability.
tender.title: S3-CL-15 ECOSTAR-S CONSOLIDATION PHASE - EXPRO+

tender.description: Objective: To design and assess the life cycle of an optimised harness including cables, connectors, and back-shell components, allmanufactured using eco-friendly processes and alternative materials.Description: Spacecraft harnesses are essential for power distribution, data transmission, and signal integrity within satellites and other spacecraft systems. However, conventional harness designs rely on materials and manufacturing techniques that have a significant environmental impact, such as PTFE (Polytetrafluoroethylene)-based insulation, gold and nickel plating, and energy-intensive production processes. The ecodesign harness initiative focuses on the development of a sustainable harness architecture, incorporating alternative materials and environmentally optimised production methods. This includes innovative approaches to conductors, insulation, jacket, connectors, accessories, tie bases, assembly processes and integration, all tailored for space qualification. This activity aims to minimise environmental impact while maintaining space-grade reliability and performance, contributing to the broader vision of sustainable space through responsible material selection, reduced emissions, and improved end-of-life strategies. A comprehensive life cycle assessment (LCA) will be performed to comparethe environmental impacts of the optimised harness against conventional designs, from raw material extraction through to end-of-life,including phases such as manufacturing, integration, launch, and decommissioning. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Trade-off analysis and environmental impact assessment. - Key environmental contributors identification. - Optimisation actions and technical feasibility. - Characterisation and LCA validation.Deliverables: Breadboard, ReportProcurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). tender.description: The frontiers for the deployment of 5G cellular networks have grown beyond the limits of the Earth's atmosphere. The 3GPP cellular technologies have become attractive for exploration missions, such as Moon or Mars, as they can provide a standardised scalable, secure, high-capacity, and reliable connectivity. For Moon, the Space Frequency Coordination Group (SFCG) has recently identified several bands for Lunar missions for the deployment of existing Earth communication protocols that includes the cellular element. In parallel to the connectivity, 5G networks can also be used to enhance the performance of navigation services fores een in LunaNet.The communication services will be primarily delivered by satellite-based solutions (already identified in the LunaNet architecture for the Moon). However, although the lunar relay satellites could technically provide surface-to-surface communications for a small number of users, such approach does not scale well as the number of users increases.To serve larger number of users, wireless cellularnetworks on the lunar surface are foreseen. With such deployments, an opportunity to offer 5G space user terminals emerges on the market. A new space-grade 5G user terminal will thus need to be developed, leveraging the technologies from 5G ground terminals, and making them available for exploration missions. This activity will design, manufacture, and test an engineering model of a 5G user terminal in FR1 for exploration missions. To achieve this, the activity willleverage on the current standards, techniques, and technologies. The activity will:- Review and consolidate the connectivity use cases of 3GPP networks in exploration missions (Moon and/or Mars)- Identify potential future exploration missions- Define and study architecture and scenarios of 5G cellular networks that could provide connectivity and enhanced navigation.- Design and implement an engineering model of 5G user equipment, including a test equipment, for connectivity in exploration missions.- Test the connectivity and positioning performance of the 3GPP networks using the developed test equipment.- Develop a roadmap to reach a flight model with integration of LunaNet navigation receiver capabilities
tender.title: 5G SPACE USER TERMINAL (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 7A.080) - EXPRO+ - RE-ISSUE

tender.description: One of the main objectives of the Space strategy for Europe is to foster a globally competitive and innovative European space sector, in particular by improving support to technological maturation for sub-systems, equipment and technologies, including in-orbit demonstration and validation activities, to reduce time to market.To ensure the European Union non-dependence and competitiveness in technologies, there is a clear need for a regular, sustainable, cost-effective and responsive In Orbit Demonstration/Validation (IOD/IOV) service in the European Union. Space flight heritage in real conditions and environment is often required to de-risk innovations such as new technologies, products, concepts, architectures, and operations techniques are they for unique or recurrent, institutional or commercial missions.On 31 March 2023, the European Commission issued a Call for Expression of Interest for In Orbit Demonstration/Validation of Experiments Needing Aggregation, open until 15 March 2027 with multiple cut-off dates. The objective is to promote European competitiveness and non-dependence by offering flight opportunities through IOD/IOV for European Experiments. The European Commission pre-selects on a regular basis a number of Experiments that may fly with the Horizon Europe In-orbit Demonstration/Validation (IOD/IOV) Service.The SmallSat Project 2026 will provide the Horizon Europe In-orbit demonstration/Validation (IOD/IOV) service with a Carrier based on European SmallSat platforms, with a system total mass (including experiments) in the range of 250 kg.The SmallSat Project 2026 Contractor will be responsible for specifying and delivering all elements required to accommodate a set of experiments selected by the European Commission, in order to bring them into space and to allow for demonstration and/or validation purposes.These activities include:-system studies, at ground and space segments levels, including accommodation analysis of theIOD/IOV Experiments on the IOD/IOV Carrier and the compatibility analysis with the available launch solutions, -input to the launch mission analysis for the launch services provider, -manufacturing, assembly, integration and test of the whole IOD/IOV spacecraft based on EU manufactured solutions including the selected experiments, -ground segment capabilities (facilities and operators) to operate the IOD/IOV mission, -management of interfaces between the different IOD/IOV Experiments and the IOD/IOV Carrier, -inputs to launcher interfaces, -transport and delivery of the IOD/IOV spacecraft to the Launch Site, -launch campaign, -launch and Early Orbit Phase (LEOP), -operations of the IOD/IOV spacecraft for maximum one year taking into account the specific needs of the experiments, -delivery of the experiments in-flight data to the experiment providers, with a right to use for ESA and EU, -decommissioning of the IOD/IOV spacecraft at the end of the operations. This project is funded by the European Union. ESA is the Contracting Authority and runs the procurement under the ESA/REG/001 rev.5 adapted as per the signed FFPA Agreement.
tender.title: IHE1-2 SMALLSAT PROJECT 2026

tender.title: IN-ORBIT SECURE TELECOM LABORATORY (ARTES 4.0 SPL 4S 3E.031) - RE-ISSUE

tender.title: LUNAR LINK REPURPOSING MISSION - PHASE 1 STUDY

tender.description: Objective: To manufacture a detector with sensitivity up to 10 um wavelength and perform its detailed performance assessment at operating temperatures down to 40 K.Description: The Near Earth Object Mission in the Infra-Red (NEOMIR hereafter) aims to overcome most of the issues encountered previously with respect to NEO (Near Earth Object) detection by regularly scanning an area not accessible by ground or other space-based NEO surveys. NEOMIR will be capable of detecting and characterizing new NEOs and - in the worst case of an imminent impactor - serve as an early warning system. The noise contribution from the detector and instrument on NEOMIR must be minimised to ensure the signal from small or distant NEOs is not lost into the background noise. These requirements drive the detector's operating temperature down towards 40 K and necessitate careful engineering of its detection layer. Within this activity,test samples of suitable detection layers will be manufactured and hybridised to readout circuits. These will be characterised downto 40 K operating temperature, assessing their performance in conditions close to those expected in NEOMIR. Where applicable, the characterisation will provide statistics on the spatial and temporal variability of device performance parameters including quantum efficiency, dark current, linearity and crosstalk. The measured performance will be provided to inform mission-level performance simulations and planning of calibration routines. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Prototype device design and manufacturing. - Test planning and test system design. - Test system assembly and commissioning. - Test campaign. - Performance assessment and conclusionsDeliverables: Prototype, ReportProcurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity)of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses
tender.title: DETECTOR ARRAY FOR LOW PHOTON APPLICATIONS IN THE 6-10 UM WAVELENGTH RANGE - EXPRO+

tender.description: General DescriptionThis activity explores the application of Approximate Computing (AxC) techniques to GNSS signal processing for reducing power consumption while maintaining acceptable accuracy. It focuses on implementing AxC in acquisition, tracking, and PVT stages of GNSS receivers. The study will identify suitable AxC methods, develop a prototype receiver supporting both exact and approximate modes, and evaluate performance in terms of power efficiency, accuracy, and correlation degradation. Test campaigns will use live and replayed GNSS data from various environments to validate the concept. For more info, visit https://navisp.esa.int/opportunity
tender.title: NAVISP-EL1-126-APPROXIMATE COMPUTING FOR LOW-POWER GNSS SIGNAL PROCESSING - EXPRO+

tender.description: ObjectivesTo develop an integrity concept leveraging Position, Velocity and Time (PVT) assurance solutions for safety critical applications.DescriptionSafety critical applications rely on integrity concepts based on protection levels and alerting schemes to bound the position error in nominal and failure scenarios under a given integrity risk. This allows estimating the worst-case user position systematically taking into account potential feared events. Similar integrity concepts and list of feared events can be developed considering the potential presence of intentional GNSS signal impairments.The Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) providers are implementing mechanism in order to protect the users from security threats such as spoofing. For instance, Galileo will provide both navigation message authentication (NMA) and ranging authentication (Commercial Service Authentication [CAS]). Therefore, the user integrity concepts will have to be expanded to define the impact of intentional interference, to specify the related feared events, and to consider the barriers provided by PVT assurance solutions.This activity aims at exploring technological enablers, algorithms and concepts for future positioning integrity concepts, which would enable safe and secure operations even in the presence of potential intentional impairments. It will investigate the contribution to the overall safety and trustworthiness provided by GNSS-based PVT assurance. Moreover, attention will be given to demonstrating that the overall target integrity can be achieved by different positioning solutions and PVT assurance techniques.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- State-of-the-art survey of integrity concepts for PVT, of PVT assurance services, and of anti-spoofing techniques,- Development of innovative security-aware concepts,- Performance assessment of the integrity concepts,- Roadmap for standardization.DeliverablesReport, Software
tender.title: SECURITY AWARE POSITION, VELOCITY AND TIME INTEGRITY CONCEPT - EXPRO+

tender.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop and test a 5G NTN dual active modem prototype with active resource management for improving link reliability and performance, whileoptimizing the space segment resources utilization.TargetedImprovements:-doubling the peak data rate compared to state of art modems.- reduction by half link outage time.Description: The need for a dual-active modem in 5G Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN) arises from the growing demand for reliable, high-performance communication links particularly inscenarios where terrestrial networks are unavailable or unreliable. A dual-active NTN modem can maintain two simultaneous satellite links, significantly reducing the risk ofoutages caused by shadowing, fading or interference. At the same time, it provides an additional communication channel that enables load balancing across space segmentnodes, helping to distribute traffic efficiently and improve peak user data rates. Active resource management is essential in this context. Strategies must be designed todynamically allocate resources based on real-time link conditions and performance metrics. These strategies should ensure that the satellite system can optimize keyperformance indicators, such as peak data rate and service availability, while minimizing the resources allocated to each link and network node (e.g. payloads). Developingcontrol plane methodologies is also a critical aspect of this solution. The control plane manages the signalling and control information required for the operation of thecommunication links. It enables the system to gather real-time measurements of links conditions, which are essential for making informed decisions about resource allocationand link management. These methodologies also provide mechanisms for communicating decisions to the network including satellites and user terminals ensuring that thesystem can adapt to changing conditions and maintain optimal performance.This activity will develop a prototype dual-active 5G modem, potentially based on open radio stacks, and implement a testbed to evaluate the prototype under realisticconditions. This testbed will include a channel emulator with multiple RF interfaces to emulate themultiple links. Channel performance as well as satellite system resourcesallocation will be tested for various operational scenarios, and both resource management methodologies and control plane techniques will be assessed.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). tender.description: The objective of this activity is to define the system requirements and the preliminary concept of a resilient communication systemoperating in non-geostationary high-altitude ellipticalorbits.TargetedImprovements: Enabling the development of high altitude inclined elliptical orbits satellite communications systems in ESA Member States for providing resilient communications.Description: Satcom satellites typically fly in Low Earth Orbit (LEO), Medium Earth Orbit (MEO), or Geostationary Orbit (GEO). However, high-altitude elliptical orbits (HEO) offer special features ofinterest to resilient and secure satcom systems. This includes in particular coverage of Europe and polar regions thanks to the large orbital inclination. Furthermore, the HEO platform isexpected to share design and development similarities with existing GEO platforms, enabling faster development and deployment.Such a HEO system can enable the rapid provision of resilient and secure satellite communications for governmental use, ensuring secure service continuity andoperational resiliencethat satisfy the short-term secure communication needs. It will consist of several satellites placed in different orbits. This approach will provide an initial layer of protection againstjamming, as a single jammer would be unable to disrupt more than one satellite. Further robustness of the system shall be provided based on anti-jamming capabilities to be investigatedin the activity.In this activity, the different governmental and commercial use cases will be investigated, and mission and user requirements will be derived.The activity will study and compare multiple orbits of interest, and define concepts of mission, system, satellite, payload, and user terminal required to achieve the desired services.System requirements will be derived. In addition to anti jamming capability, the study shall analyse and trade-off various techniques for the system to stay resilient to other kinetic andnon-kinetic impairments. System development and deployment plan, business and cost analysis and related technology roadmap shall be defined. The defined use cases and theirrelated performance shall be confirmed by means of a comprehensive mission/system simulator.A key result of the analysis will be the confirmation of the possibility to develop and rapidly deploy the satellites for the envisioned HEO system, leveraging the experience of the Europeanindustry acquired in the development of platforms and payloads for GEO orbit

tender.description: Objective: To analyse the impacts of fault propagation in spiking neural networks (SNN), propose design mitigation techniques, identify relevant neuromorphic IPs and select a baseline concept for implementation.Description: Future missions, including planetary landing, planetary exploration, docking, debris removal, space situational awareness, in-orbit servicing, etc. will need increased autonomy to address latency issues. This autonomy will rely on AI-driven computer vision and advanced computing capabilities. However,traditional neural network inferences typically require hardware platforms such as FPGAs or GPUs, which may consume anywhere from afew tens of watts to 100 watts. This high-power consumption may necessitate active cooling systems, impacting weight, volume, complexity, and ultimately resulting in additional costs and risks for missions. Safety-critical class 1 missions, including autonomous docking, autonomous landing, and autonomous rover/drone navigation, will require lower power, low footprint (pin count), scalable, and fault-tolerant hardware accelerators. Event-based processing with Neuromorphic technologies, show potential for the future of intelligent sensing, whether it involves event-based cameras, LiDAR, or radar sensors. Neuromorphic technology can address in an effectivemanner the challenge posed by edge AI, sustaining a high processing load, while keeping power consumption low (from few Watts to sub-Watt). Concrete use cases such as, autonomous landing, autonomous docking have been studied, validating Neuromorphic technology through the deployment on commercial device (COTS). Neuromorphic technology is suited for computer vision applications, planned activities should also confirm the suitability for radar as well. Few commercial IPs have shown potential in studies as explained above.However, additional work is needed to adapt a solution for space missions, ensuring low power, scalability, low pin count, and fault tolerance. Leveraging state-of-the-art neuromorphic commercially available IPs, this activity aims to propose a solution that addresses these needs effectively by designing a neuromorphic hardware accelerator using advanced rad hard ASIC technology. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Hardware accelerator specifications consolidation - selection and product roadmap definition - IP fault mitigation techniques analysis - Hardware accelerator architecture definition - Hardware accelerator design - Hardware accelerator validation / simulation.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activities in open competition limited to the-non-Large-System Integrators.For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses

tender.description: The Copernicus Sentinel-2 Next Generation space component, which is the subject of this procurement, will ensure a seamless continuation of the current Sentinel-2 first generation capabilities, whilst increasing both the quantity and quality of the products. The development of the Sentinel-2 Next Generation (Sentinel-2 NG) Space Component aims to build upon and enhance the initial observations provided by the first generation. In particular, Sentinel-2 NG (S2NG) will respond to the needs of Copernicus Services, with particular emphasis to the Land Monitoring Service (CLMS) and the Emergency Management Service (CEMS), together with, as secondary objective, the Marine Environment Monitoring Service (CMEMS). This will be characterised by enhanced spatial sampling and spectral sampling compared to Sentinel-2 first generation. S2 NG will provide observations for the next generation of operational products such as landcover maps, land-change detection maps, and geophysical properties,  together with, as secondary objective, for the next generation of operational products over a larger portion of coastal and marine waters compared to Sentinel-2. S2NG will provide quantitative evidence in support to European and global policies, including the Green Deal, the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP), the EU Forest Strategy, the EU Biodiversity Strategy, the EU Soil Strategy, the EU Water Framework and the UN SDGs. The S2NG space segment is expected to comprise of a constellation of two identical satellites (A- and B-units) flying at an altitude of approximately 650 km, in a sun-synchronous orbit. Each satellite will embark a payload comprised of the Advanced Multi-Spectral Imager (AMSI) instrument with two detection chains, one for Visible and Near-Infrared (VNIR) detection and one for the Short Wavelength Infrared (SWIR) detection, with a total of 21 bands (16 in VNIR, 5 in SWIR).The ITT for the Sentinel-2 NG Phases B2/C/D/E1 is in open competition. The ITTwill cover all spacecraft development phases (B2/C/D/E1) of the complete Sentinel-2 NG Model A Spacecraft (i.e. including Payload and Spacecraft subsystems), and the Model B Spacecraft the latter through a contractual mandatory option. This ITT will be arranged in two Contractual Phases as follows: Phase 1 will include:  - all Payload Instruments activities up to the Sentinel-2 NG Model A Instrument Preliminary Design Review, and subsequent payload advanced phase C activities up to the end of the satellite Phase B2 (PDR);- all Sentinel-2 NG spacecraft activities, including the System Requirements Review (SRR), up to and including the Satellite Preliminary Design Review (PDR); and - the procurement of relevant long lead Items (LLI) for both Sentinel-2 NG Model A and Model B Spacecraft. Phase 2 will include: - All remaining Spacecraft activities up to and including the Sentinel-2 NG Model A Spacecraft Qualification and Flight Acceptance Review (QAR).Additional information: The Invitation to Tender (ITT) will be published on ESA Star. In order to access the ITT Package, Tenderers must be registered in esa-star as potential ESA suppliers. Any Tenderer, which is not yet registered with ESA as a potential supplier, must complete the online questionnaire in esa-star, https://esastar-emr.sso. esa.int/. Further information on the registration process can be found in ESA's INDUSTRY PORTAL available at: - http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/esa-star_open_for_business - http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/How_to_do/esa-star_Registration_Process Please note that esa-star allows two levels of entity registration: "Light" and "Full". While "Light" registration will grant access to all esa-star services up to and including proposal submission, the award of ESA contracts requires "Full" registration.

tender.description: Objective: The objective is to design, develop and test an Automatic Identification System (AIS) spoofing detection system onboard the satellite for satellite-based maritime surveillance, offeringreliable AIS information with low-latency.TargetedImprovements: Reduce by half the latency of detection of non-reliable reporting vessels compared to current technologies. Decrease reliance on ground-based infrastructures by enabling onboarddetection of deceptive AIS signals.Description: With approximately 90% of international trade travelling by sea, maritime routes are becoming increasingly congested. A reliable maritime domain awareness is thus paramount toaddress critical security (e.g. submarine cables, piracy), safety (e.g. collision avoidance), economic (e.g. fleet monitoring) or environmental (e.g. illegal fishing) needs, and space-basedcomponents are critical due to the limited terrestrial systems coverage. The Automatic Identification System (AIS) is one of the main components of the current maritime domain awarenessinfrastructure, being mandated by International Maritime Organisation and enabling the reporting of vessels worldwide. However, the current AIS setup suffers from reliability issues.Vessels can arbitrarily either switch off their AIS transponder or use (or being the target of) malicious deceiving techniques such as AIS spoofing and jamming or manipulation of GNSSinformation embedded in such messages. This results in fictitious abnormal behaviours that are becoming increasingly common and causing significant disruption across entire regions.Moreover, traditional satellite-based AIS processing systems rely heavily on ground-based validation, leading to high latency in spoofing detection and reducing the effectiveness of real timecountermeasures.An onboard detection module could overcome these challenges by detecting in near real-time any AIS anomaly and initiate the mitigation countermeasures, i.e. paired with communicationto other trailing satellites or direct-to-device communication links (out of the scope of this activity), such detection system could inform users about fraudulent activities faster thantraditional surveillance systems.This activity will develop and test an onboard Automatic Identification System (AIS) spoofing detection system for satellite-based maritime surveillance, offering reliableAIS informationwith low-latency. Low latency AI-based anomaly detection and other technologies such as signal fingerprinting and deterministic algorithms will be investigated and developed.The AIS spoofing detection module shall be designed according to selecteduse cases and implemented on a software-defined radio-based payload and tested in a representativemaritime surveillance scenario to evaluate its effectiveness in detecting, localising, and mitigating AIS spoofing in real time.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. tender.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to enhance the existing Open Radio Access Network (ORAN) framework to support 5G/6G Non-Terrestrial-Network (NTN) payloads, while integrating the ORAN adaptations with conventional ground segment control centres.Targeted Improvements:1) Adapt the of Enhanced Open Radio Access Network (ORAN) interfaces to support Non-Terrestrial-Network (NTN) 5G/6G payload2) Improve the ORAN Transport network layer3) Enable the Integration of ORAN interfaces into the ground segment operations for system interoperability4) Enable new applications for NTN payloads.Description: Open Radio Access Network (ORAN) specifications are on the brink of reforming the 3GPP radio network fabric through the development and standardisation of open interfaces that provide vendor interoperability, disaggregation of radio protocol stack, access to Artificial Intelligence (AI)/Machine Learning (ML enabled Radio Intelligent Controllers (RICs) and a framework for Service Management and Orchestration (SMO). The complexity required for the management and optimisation of hybrid TN/NTN (terrestrial/non-terrestrial network) radio platforms, make ORAN an ideal candidate for handling mobility, resource allocation, quality of Service optimisation, multi-connectivity, and spectrum sharing amongothers.Currently a solid background exists to build upon and expand the current ORAN standards and interfaces to support the NTN regenerative payloads, the interworking between TN/NTN nodes and the open interface integration with ground segment Network Operations Centres (NOCs).To tackle the main challenges, this activity is expected to:1) Enhance ORAN architectures with respect to the deployment of optimised interfaces between ground and space.2) Support the adaptation of the ORAN application protocol and service models, to support the 5G/6G NTN payloads.3) Optimise the ORAN transport network association to support the satellite motion out of aspecific geographical area.4) Develop and test real and non-real time Radio Intelligent Controller (RIC) enabled AI/ML applications (xApps, rApps) for NTN node mobility, traffic steering, quality of serviceoptimisation and resource allocation.5) Integrate the ORAN open interfaces with a real or emulated/simulated NOC terminating the interface, to optimise the resource allocation of regenerative NTN nodes.6) Integrate the TN and NTN existing nodes under the same RIC and Service Management and Orchestration (SMO) platform.7) Deliver an end-to-end testbed that follows the OpenRAN workflow and demonstrate the performances for various scenarios with different service requirements.

tender.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop an on-board router with secure tagging, access control and filtering capabilities suitable to route traffic from users with different securitypriorities (e.g. commercial, governmental, etc.) to support future LEO, MEO and multi-orbit satellite communications systems.TargetedImprovements: Enabling novel capability, not existing today inESA MS, which will allow to route securely user traffic with different security constraints in large satellite communicationsconstellations.Description: Due to the increasingly shared nature of satellite communication systems, specifically at the level of the payload and inter-satellite links, there is a need for traffic filtering androuting capabilities based on different security requirements.This activity will extend the capabilities of regenerative payloads, by considering the authenticated source of the traffic and related security priorities, in order to include fine-grainedfiltering and dynamic routing. The onboard router shall be able to decide how to route packets, depending on the authenticated source (based on the validated tag), securityrequirements, destination ,type of traffic data, etc. The onboard secure routing module shall interface with a key management system managing keys used to validate theauthenticity of traffic for different entities. Algorithms specific for onboard policy-based filtering will be developed, considering various criteria for filtering and routing. In addition tofiltering based on authenticated tags, source, but also destination, packet protocol and header information, the algorithms will need to consider the varying latency anddynamic/scalable network topologies. The policy-based routing configuration will have to be dynamically reconfigurable, and shall consider, in addition to the onboard processingand memory constraints, the available inter satellite links or the available ground stations for routing decision-making. Under increased load, the router may furthermore be able torestrict the allocation of onboard resources to ensure the prioritised/efficient processing of critical traffic data. Segregated zones for management/operational purposes, as well asfor traffic with different security requirements shall be considered.The activity will design a secure on-board router enabling the filtering and routing based on the authenticated source of the traffic, integrated with a key management system. Theactivity will then implement the selected design as a payload module and perform verification and validation of the module by testing the overall resilience of the module.
tender.title: SECURE ON-BOARD AND ACCESS CONTROL ROUTER FOR FUTURE SATELLITE COMMUNICATIONS SYSTEMS (ARTES 4.0 SPL 4S 5A.097) - EXPRO+

tender.description: Objective:To develop an ADHA-compliant Instrument Controller Unit (ICU) usable standalone or with standard ADHAhardware for Earth, exploration, science, and navigation missions.Description:The ADHA (Advanced Data Handling Architecture) is a collaboration between ESA, European satellite primesand data handling equipment suppliers. It includes the definition of an architecture for data handling unit basedon standard module functions. A standard module procurement flow has been defined -- as well as astandardized backplane connector and electrical interfaces. This allows independent development ofinteroperable modules that can be connected in ADHA units. This activity aims to develop an ADHA-compatibleICU (Instrument Control Unit), with integrated Data Processing Unit(s) (DPUs). The modules target the overall control functions of an instrument with several secondary units (FEE units, mechanism control units, cryocooler unit, etc). The modules will at least include an ICU processor module, and instrument I/O module(s). The ICU processor module shall be capable to act as the system controller of an ADHA unit, running high-levelinstrument application software and providing standard high-level interfaces for connection to the spacecraftplatform units, or other instruments and implementing all the necessary functions to control peripheral ADHAmodules in the unit, including network routing capabilities. The I/O modules willcover lower-level interface functions such as additional low-speed digital interfaces (CAN, RS422/RS485, etc), and discrete interfaces(HPCs, thermistor readout, heater control, secondary power, etc) and others typically found in an ICU unit.The ICU will be basedon state-of-the-art technologies, offering a higher level of integration and performancecompared to previous generation products, and be able to perform e.g. advanced (AI-based) FDIR methodsfor the monitoring and control of a payload.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Use case analysis of instrument control units for instruments on institutional missions.- Modules requirements analysis (use case analysis, ADHA documents, ADHA ICU draft specification),including functional split between ICU processor module and I/O modules.- ICU architecture design and key components trade-off and selection.- Modules engineering model design, including electrical, firmware, and base software.- Modules engineering model manufacturing.- Modules engineering model functional and performance verification and validation.- Validation testing of modules using an ADHA backplane, in an ADHA unit rack.- Performancebenchmarks and end-to-end data handling demonstration.Deliverables: Engineering Model, Report

tender.description: Stepping Stone Missions are a new class of user driven Earth Observation missions designed to address gaps in the current EO ecosystem by delivering quality certified data and services tailored to environmental policy needs at European and global level. They build on and complement existing reference missions and infrastructures, while targeting observation domains and sampling requirements not adequately covered today. A key characteristic is their service oriented and commercially minded nature: missions are conceived from the outset to enable operational services, foster downstream applications, and evolve into scalable, privately operated constellations once their performance and utility have been demonstrated in orbit. The Stepping Stones activity focuses on conducting mission definition studies that mature candidate concepts up to a consolidated system baseline. This includes the parallel development of the space and ground segments, the definition of user oriented services, and the establishment of a robust business case demonstrating long term viability. The studies also encompass assessment of technical feasibility, verification and validation approaches, and readiness with respect to user needs, policy alignment, and commercial exploitation. Overall, the objective is to de risk and validate the end to end concepttechnical, service, and marketup to System Requirements Review level.

tender.description: The InCubed Element of the European Earth Watch Programme (InCubed) aims to accompany European economic operators in the rapid evolution of the Earth Observation market, both in Europe and globally. InCubed introduces a dedicated process within ESA Earth Observation programmes to strengthen and stimulate the development of near-to-market commercial initiatives in partnership with industry. Activities supported under InCubed include the development and/or demonstration of space assets (e.g. missions, instruments, prototype elements of EO constellations), innovative mission management solutions (including for future EO constellations), as well as the development of ground, data, and application platforms. InCubed targets commercial viability by the end of the activity (at least at minimum viable product level) and requires a substantial degree of innovation, i.e. the creation of new value within the EO commercial landscape. Commercial customer engagement is mandatory, with customers acting as beta testers and validators of the developed product or service. Customer engagement must be clearly demonstrated at both pitch and proposal stages, and letters of support or interest from potential customers are considered a strong asset. The scope of the proposed activities is defined by the economic operators themselves, in line with the objectives of InCubed. Two development cycles are available within InCubed, depending on the maturity of the concept: De-risking Cycle (typically starting from TRL 4), focusing on reducing technical and market risks;Product Development Cycle (typically starting from TRL 6), aiming at delivering a product ready for commercialisation. Under this Call for Proposals, economic operators are invited to submit their ideas via the OSIP (Open Space Innovation Platform) (ideas.esa.int), which serves as the entry point for the programme. The application process consists of the following step: Idea Pitch - Applicantssubmit and present a draft Outline proposal via OSIP to ESA (and potentially the relevant National Delegation(s)). Following a positive assessment, economic operators will be invited to submit a Proposal Part 2 (Full) in accordance with the established procedures and evaluation criteria. Activities supported under InCubed are based on a co-funding scheme, whereby economic operators contribute financially to the project, demonstrating commitment to and confidence in their business case.
