tender.description: Increasingly, advances in AI applications, models, and big data capabilities are making their way intoproductive applications. Roadmaps exist to introduce AI technologies into critical functional and operationaldomains. With new technology spin-ins like AI, cybersecurity must be accounted for, considering new attacksurfaces and vulnerabilities. Currently, no specialized approach exists forsystems with AI components,necessitating an ad-hoc approach for each system. To avoid redundant efforts, a coherent security approachfor AI applications in the space domain should be defined. Common mitigation measures for identified threatsand risks related to data and models need to be integrated into the AI lifecycle, ensuring a secure and AIenabledinfrastructure. Systems today demand increased security and even security certification. Whilesecurity approaches for non-AI systems are well understood, AI components introduce new threats. Thisactivity will guide developers in creating secure AI systems and assist project teams with certificationbasesfor AI solutions. Building on previous ESA work where security threats and mitigation measures for spacesystems were identified and considering emerging policies and regulations, this activity will develop an'MLSecOps' framework, i.e. a comprehensive set of practices and tools, processes, and datasets to addressnew vulnerabilities. These will be integrated with operational MLOps infrastructure and validated in a spacesystem context. The targeted space system applications may range from engineering aids to securitymonitoring solutions. The solution will be based on public standards and knowledge bases such as the ENISAreport "Cybersecurity of AI and Standardisation," MITRE ATLAS, and OWASP Gen AI Security Project. Theseoffer a rich list of vulnerabilities and controls without considering the required adaptations for space missionspecifics. This activity will establish a set of practices and createcommon tools for AI systems to providestandardized security features and functions, easing the certification process.
tender.title: GT1I-805GA SECURITY FRAMEWORK FOR AI APPLICATIONS (EXPRO+)

tender.description: The signal processing approach of satellite ground station back-ends is undergoing a major conceptual changeworldwide: instead of processing the signal in the back-end in the classical way with a dedicated up-/ downlinkchain, there is the more flexible approachof sampling the signal directly before transmission / after reception. Thisstep also includes the up- and down-conversion. Thereafter the data is transferred via the network using theDigital Intermediate Frequency Interoperability (DIFI) protocol and processed on a Software Defined Radio (SDR)platform (instead of a classical modem). Commercialisation of this concept is on-going on both sides: the classicalmodem/back-end providers and the providers of commercial satellite ground station services. For the latter one,the high flexibility, the easy scalability and the interoperability are only some of the key advantages. For all sidesadvantageous isthe high degree of modularity, that can be achieved with an all-digital ground station. This allows,to program dedicated modules for dedicated satellite missions, which can then be plugged into any ground station,without changing hardware components, just simply by a software update. The use of the open DIFI standardinstead of other proprietary protocols also helps avoid vendor lock-in by allowing systems from different vendorsto communicate with each other. The open DIFI standard can also be a door-opener for new andexisting vendorsto offer COTS components with the option to include custom developments according to customer requests.Furthermore, the signal digitisation right at the beginning allows for much more flexibility in terms of processing.For example, the processing could even be split between a COTS SDR and a custom developed SDR part (e.g.for a dedicated mission need(s)). This allows to take profit of low-cost COTS developments, while still maintainingall the dedicated custom developed functionalities in a separate SDRsystem. Moreover, the given flexibility of anall-digital ground station is much larger than only this and this activity will assess additional possibilities which anall-digital ground station could provide. Additionally, it will also show in which areas there are still limitations toovercome.This activity is complementary to the TDE activity, T712-703GS - Ground Station Backend Architecture with High-Rate Sampling and Software Defined Radio, for a very limited all digital ground station.
tender.title: GT17-883GS ALL-DIGITAL GROUND STATION

tender.description: The objective: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture and test a 12bit direct conversion receiver module covering the full Ka-band with significant reduced power consumption in comparison to current state of the art.Targeted Improvements:- Enabling a European source of low power direct conversion Ka-band receivers.- Factor 5 reduction of power consumption compared to the State of the Art.Description: Today's flexible telecommunication satellites require receivers operating at higher frequencies and over a wider bandwidth than in the past, with a complex RF chain and lossyharnesses. A trend towards highly integrated solutions using direct sampling receivers compatible with Software Defined Radios (SDRs) is one solution, but the power consumption of these direct sampling architectures can be prohibitive for some applications. The available direct conversion receivers in Ku-band and Ka-band have power consumption figuresin excess of several Watts and limited conversion accuracy, constraining the application areas where these could be used for space telecommunication applications. A direct conversion receiver system in a single package integrating the Analog to Digital Converter (ADC) in the advanced semiconductor technology and using a time-interleaved ADCarchitecture can achieve the desired lower power consumption and higher conversion accuracy.This activity will develop a prototype wideband ADC with high-speed track-and-hold circuit, implemented as a System-in-Package (SiP) RF to digital front-end module including digital processing features, operating in upper Ka-band. Available State-of-the-Art low-power wideband ADC will be assessed, and a trade-off analysisperformed to determine the optimum RF chain architecture (including the track-and-hold with digital processing engine and high-speed interfaces) suitable for wideband SDRs operating in full Ka-bandapplications. The breadboard will be designed to meet key performance requirements in terms of power consumption (<500mW per channel), bandwidth, and input frequency. The noise and linearity performance shall be measured to determine suitability for a range of SDR scenarios also considering synchronisation and clock jitter requirements. The breadboard shall be tested in a representative RF chain architecture in a laboratory environment, to demonstrate direct sampling at upper Ka-band frequencies and assess viability for V/W band applications. Additionally, radiation tolerance shall be demonstrated by analysis to assess suitability of the low-power ADC for future applications in space.

tender.description: ObjectivesDeriving algorithms and their optimal settings for enabling real-time highly accurate and reliable navigation based on GNSS carrier phase measurements exploiting quantum optimization algorithms.DescriptionHigh Accuracy with GNSS requires usage of phase measurements, which are ambiguous. Carrier phase Ambiguity Resolution (AR) is a stochastic process which requires a minimizationsearch for the correct ambiguities which can require a very large search to find the correct solution.In recent years, a series ofquantum algorithms for mathematical optimisation has been formulated which could be exploited to replace the classical approaches, such as those currently in use for GNSS AR. Quantum least squares can be used to perform Integer Least Square minimization, which would speed up the processing time for searching the right solution even in a larger search space. A fast and accurate solution of theGNSS carrier phase AR problem by means of quantum optimisation, in particular, would enable real-time Highly Accurate Reliable and Precise (HARP) positioning based on GNSS carrier phase positioning with integrity capabilities for users, achieving stringent positioning bounding with a very high level of confidence.This activity will define algorithms and their optimal settings for quantum optimization algorithms enabling real-time highly accurate and reliable navigation based on GNSS carrier phase measurements. The activity will rely on the quantum computers or simulators nowadays available to users as free prototypes from various companies, anticipating the advent of Quantum Processing Units which could become operational in the mid to long term.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Definition of the quantum optimisation algorithms for GNSS AR;- Prototyping of quantum navigation estimator for PPP-AR users;- Prototyping of quantum carrier phase AR and identifying its implication on integrity related to achieving HARP positioning;- Trading off of the number of qubits and the achievable performance.DeliverablesReport, Software
tender.title: HIGHLY ACCURATE RELIABLE AND PRECISE GNSS POSITIONING WITH QUANTUM OPTIMIZATION - EXPRO+

tender.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop advanced and post-quantum Subscriber Identity Module (SIMs) for 5G/6G NTN. The focus is to improve user anonymity for robust non-terrestrialnetworks (NTNs) used for governmental applications which have a more urgent need for post-quantum anonymity protection than the commercial market. These SIMs shall implementsecurity improvements of the part of the primary authentication protocol which is implemented in the SIM. Additionally, the corresponding SIM provisioning infrastructure and the corenetwork responsible for the communication with the SIMs will be developed.TargetedImprovements: Enablinga European or Canadian source for robust NTN SIM (Physical Universal Integrated Circuit Card (UICC) or Embedded UICC (eUICC)) for 5G/6G satellite constellation withhardened primary authentication protocolDescription: Current 5G Universal Subscriber Identity Modules (USIMs) to be used in Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN) for Satellite Communication (SATCOM) terminals lack adequate protectionagainst user tracking when assuming a quantum attacker. While 3GPP is working on the migration to post-quantum cryptography, the privacy needs in governmental NTN networks arehigher than in usual mobile networks and regulatory needs will require the full post-Quantum migration as early as 2030 for governmental communication solutions. An appropriatesolution therefore needs to be developed earlier than the 3GPP timeline foresees.The activity will design, develop and test prototypes of advanced 5G/6G USIMs integrating security improvements to the primary authentication protocol (user tracking enhancements inNTNs and anticipated regulatory requirements for post-quantum cryptography), with all components adhering to GSMA/ETSI security standards and targeting Common Criteria evaluationto prepare for future accreditation.The activity will evaluate two implementation paths to address this need: Physical Universal Integrated Circuit Card (UICC) development, potentially as an applet on an existing smartcard platform, or Embedded UICC (eUICC) with appropriate SIM profiles for multi-provider service access. Post-Quantum Key Exchange Management (KEM) implementations on smartcards prove the technical feasibility of implementing such protocols in the UICC approach.The activity will be implemented in a phased approach.The first phase will study the implementation of post quantum security in the authentication protocol and perform a trade-off analysis between the two implementation paths. It will designand develop an initial prototype of the USIM and provisioning infrastructure compatible with standardised 3GPP interfaces between USIM and Mobile Equipment and perform the designof the security functions of the Core network solution to interoperate with the USIM. Phase 1 deliverables consist of architecture and design documents, initial documents to prepare thecertification, software prototype and adapted core network functions to interoperate with the software. The budget for Phase 1 is up to 700 kEuros.In the second phase, the activity will further develop and test the USIM components (UICC or eUICC), create the complete SIM provisioning infrastructure, and develop and test the corenetwork security functionsincluding the Subscriber Identifier De-concealing Function (SIDF) to support enhanced authentication of the USIM to the network. Phase 2 deliverables includethe adaptation of smart card including applet design and SIM printer or chip development for eUICC and refined certification preparation.During the activity, dissemination towards 3GPP standardisation shall be performed to ensure futureindustry adoption.
tender.title: ANONYMITY AND POST QUANTUM SECURITY SUBSCRIBER IDENTITY MODULE (SIM) TECHNOLOGY FOR 5G/6G NTN (ARTES 4.0 SPL 4S 3D.040)

tender.description: Objective:To develop and test a model for a digital twin of attitude and orbit control system (AOCS) sensors as well as toassess compatibility of this multi-physics model-based digital twin with on-board self-calibration employing datadriven techniques and withthe simplification of ground verification processes of new satellite platforms.Description:Advances in model based engineering and digital twin (DT) development has led to growth in the interest of multiphysic modelling of space systems, including, for example, AOCS sensors. The AOCS sensor DTs includefunctional and performance behaviour, complemented by physical behaviour (thermal, power, electronic, etc.), as well as failure and degradation modes. This detailed modelling is based on analytic and background suppliermodels. The emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) / machine learning (ML) combined techniques, potentiallyaugmented with analytical a priori knowledge, offer the potential to improve the overall accuracy and validity ofthis modelling, together with a specific interest for statistical interpretation in the case of mass production (sensors for constellations, for example, gyros, star trackers, sun sensors). These new engineering techniques aimed at better fidelity in the AOCS sensor modelling offer the prospect of extending the benefits to on-board performance, for example, by adapting these techniques to the ultimate AOCS sensor calibration: self-calibration on board the spacecraft (e.g. constellation or low-cost platform). The following techniques and use cases will be studied:- Digital Twin for AOCS sensors, preferably from sensors used on platform series: architecture; interoperabilityneeds, multi-physic modelling trade-off and key components; use of data-driven techniques (AI/ML) to populate the DT models; statistical interpretation and validation of AOCS sensor performance (mass manufacturing, groundself-calibration based on sample measurements and statisticextrapolation).- Use of ground models and knowledge for on-board self-calibration; data fusion techniques for on-board use to consolidate ground self-calibration with flight measurements, autonomously; autonomous verification of on-board self-calibration (fault detection).This activity will bring tools, methods, and processes for increasing the end-to-end autonomous handling of AOCS sensorsin the platform development and verification chain. It includes predictive maintenance monitoring to inform on the overall health status and to prevent anomalies/failures. This activity aims at providing digital data and models to improve knowledge of the units in flight, allowing correction and improvement by the supplier and better integration in model-based system engineering (MBSE) or digital production.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Define the system into which the deliverable items will be integrated, establish the end user requirements andquantify the advantages of utilising the new items with respect to state-of-the-art alternatives.- Define a complete, self-standing and traceable set of technical requirements for the deliverable items.- Select the technical baseline that offers the best potential to achieve the activity objectives.- Detailed design and demonstrate, by appropriate analyses, simulations, tests or other means, that it cansatisfy the technical requirements.- Establish all detailed plans necessary to successfully implement and test the deliverable items and verify theircompliance to the technical specifications.- Implement the deliverable items, quantify their performances by means of a suitable test campaign anddemonstrate compliance to the technical requirements.

tender.description: Sustainable mineral resource management involves the responsible extraction, use, and conservation of mineral resources to meet present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet theirs. It emphasizes efficient mining practices, minimizing environmental impacts, and restoring ecosystems after extraction. An important component of this approach is the use of Earth observation technologies, which allow the detection of (critical earth) minerals, continuous monitoring of mining activities, land degradation and water quality. The development of novel EO solutions and tools improve transparency, support better decision-making, andhelp detect unsustainable practices in near real time. Combined with recycling, resource efficiency, and strong environmental policies, Earth observation enhances the ability to balance economic development with environmental protection and social responsibility,ensuring long-term sustainability of mineral resources.

tender.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, develop, launch and test autonomous and intelligent avionics enabling satcomconstellation satellites to operate autonomously across multiple environmental conditions in Low Earth Orbit (LEO). Breadboarding and in-orbit testing of critical platform functions including health monitoring, orbital control and resourcemanagement will be carried out. As part of the in-orbit experiment, a payload technology demonstrator will be developed to experiment with innovative approaches of autonomous payload configuration and control.Targeted Improvements: Enabling autonomous operation and reconfiguration of a satellite in a range of orbital LEO environments. This entails orbital control, platform resource management, health monitoring capability, autonomous decision-making capability and autonomous communication to ground.Description: Satellite operators currently face limitations when relying on single orbits (e.g. geostationary or low Earth orbit) for communications. These limitations affect system performance, resilience, and service continuity, especially in the aviation, maritime, governmental, and remote enterprise networks sectors. There is a growing need for an intelligent on-board control system that is capable to operate constellation satellites in multiple orbital LEO altitudes and environments. Such avionics systems must operate reliably across multiple orbital shells under varying environmental conditions, such as radiation, power constraints, and thermal fluctuations, particularly in very low earthorbits. Developing avionics that could autonomously detect the need for adaptation/changes of orbit and will enable:- autonomous multi-orbit operation- orbital transfer- repositioning of satellites in fleet and constellations.The activity will develop an intelligent avionics module enabling autonomous operation. An experimental satcom platform and payload will be developed and an in-orbit experiment will be carried out across a large range of space environmental conditions (e.g. eclipse period, radiation levels, thermal loads) in LEO.The activity will be implemented in a phased approach:Phase 1 (budget up to 2 MEuro) will design, develop and integrate an intelligent avionics module to full engineering model enabling autonomous satellite operations.  Phase 1 will develop and test:- autonomous operations logic that enables real-time system response to varying environmental conditions- adaptive AOCS and GNC functions to adapt to different orbits- health monitoring and diagnostic decision-making- autonomous TTC communication to ground.Phase 2 will develop the flight engineering model of the avionics module. A satcom experimental payload will be developed tosupport experimentation with intelligent, autonomous payload reconfiguration (e.g. transmit power, beam pointing, coverage change, temperature stabilisation, etc.) to maintain services during dynamic events such as orbital transfers and changes to operational space environmental and resilience response to sub-system failure. Avionics and payload will be integrated into a satellite. Phase 2 will launch and operate experiments in multiple LEO altitudes and environmental conditions.
tender.title: IN-ORBIT EXPERIMENT OF INTELLIGENT AUTONOMOUS AVIONICS ENABLING MULTI-ENVIRONMENT SATCOM SATELLITE OPERATION IN LEO (ARTES AT 3E.033) (ON DELEGATION REQUEST)

tender.description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop and test a multi-wavelength, multi-port light source for space applications. The source will need to be energyefficient, compact and able to generate continuous-wave multiple wavelengths output.TargetedImprovements:The multi-wavelength laser is needed to enable high-speed and high-density co-packaged optics data interconnects for space applications.Description: Modern telecommunication satellites use onboard digital processors to meet growing traffic demands. These high throughput processors can handle Tbpsof intra-processor traffic thanks to the adaptation of optical interconnects in placeof traditional electrical harness. When co-packaged photonics becomeavailable for use in space regenerative processors, they will enable even higher data rate on-board interconnects with optical I/Os. This, in turn, will requirean external continuous-wave wavelength division multiplexing laser source for operation. The present activity aims at developing such a laser source forspace use.This activity will develop and test the multi-wavelength source. The source packaging and physical configuration shall consider two variants of opticaloutput; a configuration where each wavelength can be coupled to an individual fibre, and a configuration where multiple wavelengths can be multiplexedto a single fibre output. The environmental effects on the multi-wavelength source output stability should be assessed. The laser source engineeringmodel, together with its electrical and thermal control, should be developed for satellite on-board operation. A definition and demonstration of the opticalparameters together with the measurement methods forthe source used onboard a satellite shall be produced. The parameters should include the numberof wavelengths, wavelength grid spacing, output power, relative intensity noise, side mode suppression ratio and linewidth.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. tender.description: Objective: To develop and refine a power efficient Fast Fourier Transform IP Core for FPGA/ASIC implementationDescription: This activity focuses on the design, development and testing of a Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) block to be used in space applications, which is to be developed as a configurable, reusable IP Core. A reusable IP Core is a hardware model, normally described in VHDL, which is fully verified and can be used as a building block in designs for several targets, such as FPGAs from different vendors or as an ASIC, providing savings in mission costs and development times. The developed IP shall be able to solve complex FFT / inverse FFT; convolve and correlate vectors in frequency domain, with a length up to 32768 points, gain and phase correction, filtering, etc. Several applications will benefit from such an IP Core: - Active Microwave Remote Sensing: Radar Onboard Processing, such as SAR Image Formation, RFI Detection, Compression - Passive Microwave Remote Sensing: Hyperspectral Radiometers (channelisation, RFI detection), Compression Although FFT IPs are available commercially, fine spectral resolution together with high sampling rate (e.g. direct conversion) leads to long FFT lengths, which may not be available in commercial IPs. Furthermore, many of these applications require high-throughput, e.g. channelisation, together with real-time constraints. These requirements give raise to needs regarding adequate standardized Input/Output interfaces (such as AXI-Stream buses) as well as efficient FFT architectures, to cope with the throughput. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Specifications of the FFT IP Core, taking into account the different application needs. - Description of the IP core in VHDL. The IP shall be configurable. - Development of a tool that helps the user configure and generate the IP core based on specific mission requirements. - Verification and Synthesis on relevant space FPGA devices. - Laboratory demonstrator The developed IP core will be offered to future missions and projects as part of the ESA IP Core's portfolio, which already includes a catalogue of more than 20 cores which comprise typical digital functions used in space applications (TMTC, EDAC, SpaceWire, CAN, LEON2-FT, OBDH, etc).Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). tender.description: Objective:To develop a technology independent soft IP (Intellectual Property) core that complies with the aerospace profile of TSN(Time Sensitive Networking).Description:TSN (Time-Sensitive Networking) and TTE (Time Triggered Ethernet) are the two technologies that allow to deliver determinism and quality of service on top of standard Ethernet networks. Since TTE can be considered  relatively closed technology (i.e. proprietary solution, patents pending on the technology), since a few years TSN is emerging as a potential successor of that technology. TSN is IEEE supported set of standards that implements wide range of quality of services (i.e. reliability, determinism, mixed criticality traffic, redundancy, time synchronization) on top of the standard Ethernet protocols. TSN benefits from Ethernet Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) tools/ecosystem, it is free of patents and is being introduced step-by step in industrial applications (automotive/industrial) and aerospace domain (IEEE P802.1DP - TSN for Aerospace Onboard Ethernet Communications). Although TSN is very successful in the automotive/industrial sector, in space applications TSNis still being considered as low TRL technology. Many current and future Exploration and Space Transportationmissions are considering Ethernet-based networks for the data-handling communication bus. Having thistechnology available for future ESA missions is seen as a key driver for future missions. The aim of this activity Is to develop an IP core that contains the core functionalities of Time-Sensitive Networking needed for space applications. Although the set of TSN standards is very wide, there are several on-going activities aiming attailoring of TSN for space applications. Having an TSN IP tailored to space applications could be considered asa key enabler of this technology in future ESA and national missions.The following technical aspects shall be considered:- Development of End-system IP Core. Switch IP core is out of scope of this activity- One or two Ethernet ports shall be supported.- Host integration: AXI4 lite for registers and IP configuration, and AXI4 stream for packet data- The IP shall support 10/100/1000Mbps speeds. 10Gbps is considered optional.- Compatible and configurable with various PHY interfaces (i.e. MII/GMII/RGMIII).- To be developed as technology independent VHDL.- To be implemented and validated in 2 FPGA/ASIC technologies (preferable NG-Ultra/Ultra300 andMicrochip Polarfire).This activity encompasses the following tasks:- TSN IP core requirements identification and development of the high-level architecture of the TSN soft IP core.- Prototype development and integration into a representative Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) based network platform.- Verification and validation targeting high speed use cases- TSN soft IP core release and related documentation.Deliverables: Prototype, Report, SoftwareApplication/Need Date: Exploration and Space Transportation missions. Mission Classification: alpha, beta,gamma, delta
tender.title: DETERMINISTIC ETHERNET SPACE TIME-SENSITIVE NETWORKING SOFT IP CORE - EXPRO+

tender.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop a European g-NodeB (gNB) hardware and software protocol stack architecture for regenerative NGSO satellite with a fully European signal processing platform, i.e., both hardware and softwareTargeted Improvements: Enabling a European full gNB in Space for regenerative 5G/6G broadband satellite systems not existing today in ESA Member StatesDescription: The 3GPP standardisation group has defined the necessary features and enhancements in 5G mobile broadband systems tosupport non-terrestrial network (NTN) since Release 17 in 2022. The upcoming 6G NTN integration into the terrestrial telecom systemenables new features such as:a. Seamless interoperability between terrestrial and satellite networks;b. Direct-to-device connectivity without specialised satellite terminals in FR 1 (i.e., <7GHz);c. Ubiquitous connectivity across geography;d. Broadband servicesfor aviation, maritime, and cross-border mobility;e. AI-Native networking to optimise beam management, manage mobility, and dynamically allocate spectrum across the multi-layered satellitenetwork.However, today no European solution exists for a full gNB signal processing hardware platform and software protocol stack as needed for 5G/6Gregenerative NTN payloads.This activity will develop a European gNB hardware and software protocol stack architecture for regenerative NGSO satellite with a fully European signalprocessing platform, i.e., both hardware and software. The gNB shall be able to support high throughput 5G/6G connectivity either in S-band spectrum(e.g., up to 50Mbit/s) or in Ka-band spectrum (e.g., up to 1Gbit/s).The activity will: Develop a concept of an efficient signal processing hardware and software protocol stack architecture for a European gNB implementation for regenerative NGSO satellites. Identify a suitable European signal processing platform and characterise relevant functional blocks of the signal processing hardware. A laboratory breadboard will be developed together with electrical ground support equipment (EGSE) suitable to performradiation characterisation including Single Event Effects (SEE), Displacement Damage (DD), and Total Ionizing Dose (TID). A radiation mitigation approach shall be developed and implemented using a combination of software- and hardware-based solutions to compensate for identified critical performance impacts. The devicewith the applied radiation mitigation measures will be radiation tested,and the performance will be compared to the unmitigated hardware performance. Carry out analysis and concept trade-offs to ensurethehigh throughput connectivity and minimised power consumption per MHz in the selected band (S-band or Ka-band)Identify and assess relevant in-orbit experiment considerations.

tender.description: Objective: To develop a breadboard of a radiation detection unit based on Advanced Data Handling Architectures (ADHA) in order to minimise on-board resources, while improving the integration and deployment.Description: The Agency has had success developing and flying radiation monitors, starting with the REM in the 90's, the SREM in the 2000s, and the EMU and NGRMs since 2017. These monitors have all been self contained and externally mounted, with masses and power requirements exceeding 1 kg and 2 W - low resource, butnot insignificant. Some of these instruments have housed dosimeters, but none have provided measurements within the other spacecraft units. At the moment, there are no low resource radiation monitors available capable of integration within the spacecraft and its units where the sensitive systems are located and capable to provide useful, unparalleled feedback to satellite operations. The benefits include enabled monitoring of the spacecraft health, and providing useful operational diagnostics, and accurate information on the environment. Radiation monitors are the first modules to be discarded during phase A of design due to additional mass and power budget constraints. This disrupts the huge potential of in-orbit data collection, which affects radiation model accuracy and uncertainty a measure, Radiation monitor will allow to manage approach to radiation effects, potentially extending mission lifetimes and opening the door to widespread use of COTS. It is envisaged that this should become standard on all platforms as part of S/C 'health' data - as is already done with thermal measurements. In order to enhance the European competitiveness for LEO applications for mid-size satellites, it is aimed to design and test a portfolio of standardized dosimeters and memories. By including the radiation monitors in the Advanced Data Handling architecture (ADHA), standardized, interchangeable, and inter-operable electronics modules equipped with the latest generation of microelectronics components can be integrated within the spacecraft units. Components and commercialprocesses from European foundries and manufacturers shall be baselined for dose measurements. Several configuration can be considered: detection unit embedded into each ADHA board, detection unit placed at different point of ADHA or to be considered as a standalone board. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - A trade-off shall be made between of the different solutions considered -Breadboarding and functional testing - Total ionising Dose and SEE testing - Roadmap to fully characterise and fly European memories once they become availableDeliverables: Breadboard, Report

tender.description: Today, mission ground segment systems face increasingly sophisticated and fast-movingcyber threats that can evade static or rule-based detection tools and overwhelm traditionalrecovery procedures. As attacks grow more pervasive, dynamic and subtle, currentapproaches, such as rule-based or ticket driven responses struggle to react at the requiredspeed, resulting in prolonged attacker dwelltime and potential disruption of critical missionoperations, if an attack is detected at all.Real-time automated responses or self-healing' mechanisms, such as fall-back tosecure/minimum configurations, runtime policy/rule change, trusted state reconstitution, orrapid tear-down and re-deploy of compromised systems, can reduce the time required tocontain threats. The aim is to reduce attacker dwell time and maintain service continuityduring otherwise high impact incidents. This activity addresses that gap by developing anddemonstrating a proof-of-concept autonomous self-healing architecture tailored to thecritical mission operations ground segment. It will provide an adaptive resilience mechanismaddressing detection, isolation and recovery with an emphasis on service continuity. Moderntechnologies and techniques are to be explored including:- declarative infrastructure as code for cloud-agnostic redundancy and recovery automation- decoupled micro-service isolation and zero-trust architectures- secure root of trust and immutable system configuration restoration- failure prediction- adaptive response mechanisms leveraging machine learning.The proof-of-concept demonstrator will be integrated into a multi-mission, cloud nativeground segment scenario, leveraging existing (Cyber) Security Operations Centres((C)SOC) monitoring and diagnostic capabilities to ensure operational relevance. It willdemonstrate end to enddetection, isolation, and recovery in the context of missionmonitoring and control systems operating in the loop.

tender.description: Objective:The objective of this study is to develop a system concept extending High-throughput Optical Network (HydRON) services to High-Altitude Pseudo-Satellites (HAPS) and their networks. To identify the technology gaps as well as the required development roadmap including estimations of schedule and costs.Targeted Improvements:To enable the connectivity of HAPS to an evolution of the satellite optical network system.Description:High-Altitude Pseudo-Satellites (HAPS) will play the role of an intermediate, airborne layer in a multi-domain/orbit communications architecture in line with the optical-6G concept. HAPS operate in the stratosphere at altitudes of 15 to 50 km, where they can maintain a near-stationary position for weeks or even months at a time. A single HAPS cancreate a wide-area communication cell that provides reliable connectivity to remote or rural areas where building traditional terrestrial infrastructure is uneconomical. A satellite-to-HAPS optical link can serve as a high-bandwidth feeder link, backhauling data from the HAPS to the satellite network and then to the terrestrial network, avoiding the need for a ground gateway in an inaccessiblelocation. HAPS can conduct long-term surveillance or monitoring missions over a specific area of interest, providing a significantadvantage over LEO satellites which only pass over a given point for a few minutes at a time. With an optical link, a HAPS can uplinkreal-time, high-resolution imagery and sensor data to a satellite (or another HAPS), enabling rapid analysis for applications like border security, environmental monitoring, or situational awareness. In the event of a natural disaster that destroys ground-basedcommunication networks, HAPS can be rapidly deployed to provide a temporary but persistent communications hub. The optical link to an optical backbone network like HydRON ensures that the HAPS remains connected to the global network, providing critical communicationcapabilities for first responders and civilians.The activity shall investigate user needs, requirements, and system concepts for HAPS-space bidirectional optical communications, to upgrade the HydRON System with an airborne layer. Technology gaps and relatedtechnology roadmaps shall be identified and addressed for any critical technology, including optical terminals. The system shall consider the management of cloud-blockage by combining space communications with e.g. a HAPS-to-HAPS free-space network or hybrid communications in RF. The concept shall consider the combination of security sensitive communications with logistic traffic. Finally, the activity shall propose a demonstrator concept where the relevant technology as well as the operational concept can be verified. The activity will also contribute to the evolution of ESTOL.

Ranging from a mere on-board performance demonstration over a singleoptical downlink scenario to a dual downlink case, different scenarios for in-orbit performance tests shall be carried out. The source performance degradationin orbit shall be measured together with in-orbit assessment of critical/sensitive items. To this end an appropriate in-situ monitoring and measurementtestbed is to be developed and operated in-orbit.

Launch and spacecraft re-entry effects onthe atmosphere are known gaps to fulfil these requirements. This results in significant uncertainty andsystematic exclusion of such effects when developing materials on the basis of sustainable performance.Previous and ongoing Discovery activities, Insights into the Chemistry of Atmospheric Re-entry of JunkedSpacecraft (ICARUS) and Impacts of space Debris ablation on Earth's Atmospheric System (IDEAS), havehighlighted the potential importance of ablation products in the atmosphere while established initial modellingapproaches and experimental validation capabilities.The proposed activity addresses this critical knowledge gap by developing a consolidated experimental andmodelling framework to characterise emissionsfrom spacecraft re-entry and integrate these into atmosphericand design assessment tools. This will enable the incorporation of atmospheric impacts into Life CycleAssessment (LCA) and support both Ecodesign and Design-for-Demise (D4D) decision making. Such aframework would be the first worldwide.The activity encompasses the following tasks:- Identify representative launcher and spacecraft demise-critical materials as well as Space Debris Particles(SPSs)- Propose material characterization factors (e.g. Ozon Depletion metrics, radiative forcing proxies) andassociated quantification methodology- Refine methods to allow observation and characterization of particles generated during the vaporizationphase of selected materials- Demonstrate validation tests under realistic atmospheric re-entry conditions (e.g. Thermal, pressure andflow conditions) measuring and linking ablation fluxes to downstream chemical compositions- Parametrization and modelling of datasets for integration into re-entry and atmospheric chemistryclimatemodels-Define uncertainty and applicability ranges for model use- Formulate recommendations for standardised testing procedures to support the continuous developmentand population of material datasets.Procurement Policy: C(3) = Activity restricted to SME  RD organisations, preferably in cooperation. tender.description: Summary Description The proposed activity is will support the preparation for the ERASE Phase A. ERASE aims to prepare the removalof large, non-cooperative and unprepared objects in low Earth orbit, initially considering Metop and Sentinel-1 targets (starting with METOP-A and S1B, both being decommissioned), thereby supporting ESA's Space Safety Programme and the transition towards a circular economy in space. This activity will establish and demonstrate ground-based laser-ranging measurement, modelling and analysis capabilities to characterise the attitude state and tumbling behaviour of non-cooperative, unprepared targets, with initial focus on Metop and Sentinel-1 targets. The output is essential and urgent for the ERASE Phase A study. Without this information available at the start of Phase A, there is a risk that the technical feasibility of the mission is incorrectly assessed. The target spin rate is adesign driver for the servicer delta-V and operations timeline, the relative navigation subsystem, and the robotic capture sizing and loads. The spin-axis orientation drives the safe approach direction and the capture strategy. In addition, the probability of very low spin-rate cases must be understood, as such cases may lead to long durations in unfavourable attitude conditions for target power generation, thermal control and ground contact. The challenge is that the targets are not prepared with cooperative markers or laser retro-reflectors that would facilitate attitude reconstruction. The attitude state must therefore be reconstructed from non-cooperative laser-ranging observables, making use of time-of-flight/range measurements, return-signal characteristics, pass geometry, target geometry, known or estimated surface properties, and attitude-dynamics modelling. Where beneficial, the laser-ranging data maybe complemented by passive optical or radar observations.The activity will assess the feasibility, achievable accuracy and uncertainty of attitude determination and dynamics-based propagation from ground. It will characterise and propagate target dynamics, in particular spin rate and spin-axis orientation, and will provide statistically meaningful uncertainty envelopes for ERASE Phase A design trade-offs. The activity will also prepare the capability to perform repeated attitude characterisation campaigns in support of ERASE. The attitude state of non-cooperative targets may evolve over time due to environmental torques and target-specific dynamics; therefore, measurements may be required not only during the present feasibility phase, but also before launch, to confirm that the target conditions remain within the design assumptions, and potentially at intermediate points during mission preparation. A dedicated task will assess the applicability of the developed measurement and modelling methods to a broader range of large, unprepared, non-cooperative low Earth orbit targets beyond Metop and Sentinel-1, identifying the key target properties, observation conditions and limitations that determine feasibility.

tender.description: Objective: To design PNT techniques and algorithms relying on only 1 and 2 LEO satellites in view, based on the optimised fusion ofall the available estimations along time.Description: The use of LEO-based systems on top of current GNSS systems (in MEO orbits) is being considered to improve the achievable user performances, in particular in challenging user scenarios. To ensure that at least3 or 4 satellites are in view by any user on ground, a much larger number of LEO satellites than for MEO is required to be used inthis case. In this context, it is of high interest to investigate techniques exploiting signals received by LEO satellites when only 1 and 2 LEO satellites are in view by a ground user. This would enable, for example, to exploit LEO satellites with reduced constellations with a limited available number of satellites visible, and/or while a full LEO-PNT constellation is still being deployed. Theobjective of this activity is to design PNT techniques and algorithms relying on only 1 and 2 LEO satellites in view,, including transitions between 1 and 2 satellites, based on the optimised fusion of all the available estimations along time, including at least:- ToA (Time-of-Arrival), FoA (Frequency-of-Arrival) and AoA (Angle-of-Arrival)-like estimations; - Multi-epoch / synthetic apertureprocessing solutions exploiting the fast satellite geometry change; and, additionally, if introducing benefits to the above : - Clock coasting; - Inertial sensors measurements; - DEM (Digital Elevation Model)/height sensors ; The suitability of the proposed solutions is aimed to be assessed based both on simulations and real data. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Define and design innovative techniques and algorithms in the areas identified above; - Develop the required tools/software for the assessment/test of the innovative techniques and algorithms; - Assess/test the different techniques and algorithms in realistic simulated conditions, and with real signals from LEO satellites; - Identify the most promising techniques/algorithms based on the results obtained;- Propose the way-forward to further mature each of the promising techniques/algorithms identified.Procurement Policy: C(2) = Activities in open competition, where a significant participation of non-LSI is requested. tender.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop bundle protocol and network stack, enabling automatic high-volume end-to-enddata distribution within integratedRF and optical networks. The testbed shall be developed to test networks feature heterogenous links, e.g. in terms of data rates or latencies, and includeend users, mission and payload control centres, optical and RF ground stations and space data relay systems.TargetedImprovements:Standardised data distribution irrespective of RF or optical communication.Reduced ground segment complexity (single system for RF and optical).Automatic network-based distribution.Increased E2E data delivery accountability leveraging unified reporting.Description: The need for hybrid (optical and RF) networks is due to the volumeof data transferred by satellites 00that is ever increasing. Optical communicationpotentially combined or augmented with RF communication at higher frequencies is supporting high or very high data rates. The distribution of this datais non-trivial and faces several challenges like non-permanent connectivity and asymmetric data rates in space and on ground just to name a few. It ishighly desirable to take a reliable and interoperable end-to-end approach with a common addressing scheme to cross organisational boundaries whilebeing able to monitor and manage the overall process of data distribution.The activity will develop an integrated optical andRF scalable high-volume data distribution testbed (demonstrating beyond 1 TB per downlink) based onDisruption Tolerant Networking (DTN). The activity will develop combined software and hardware. The testbed will be tested for high speed DTN nodesconnected over Wide Area Networks, emulating end users, control centres, and ground stations connecting with simulated spacecraft. It will includemonitoring and control aspects of individual nodes and DTN Network Management. The activity will allow the gathering of valuable experience in arepresentative environment and will address the problem of reliable and efficient data distribution in heterogenous ground networks and prepares theexpected deployment of DTN in space nodes in the future.

tender.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to investigate mission concepts for entanglement distribution QUAntum SpAce netwoRk (QUASAR) in the context ofQuantum Information Networks. The aim is to define preliminary requirements of the in-orbit-experiment, involving a space segment and at least twodistant ground stations, required to verify entanglement distribution from space.TargetedImprovements:The targeted improvement is to mature the quantum payload concept definition and mission requirement, to improve the viability of the in-orbitexperiment of satellite entanglement distribution with the current and near-future technology.Description: The development of Quantum Information Networks (QIN) is rapidly increasing, driven largely by the expansion of terrestrial fibre networks. However,long distance quantum communication remains fundamentally constrained by fibre losses. To overcome this limitation, the integration of a space segmentis essential. A critical step towards this integration is the execution of an in-orbit experimentto validate space-to-ground entanglement distribution. Thismission would represent a major milestone in demonstrating the satellites' role in the expansion of Quantum Information Networks.The proposed activity aims to prove the technical feasibility of space-based QIN. Consequently, this would strengthen the market potential by confirmingsatellite-to-ground entanglement distribution capabilities. The main tasks of this activity will: identifying the critical elements involved in the space and ground segments (for technical and economic suitability); exploring the various possible system concepts by modelling to determine possibilities, characteristics or the criticality of certain elements; comparing these concepts against the needs, to determine levels of uncertainty andrisk; estimating the technical and industrial feasibility; identifying, for each possible system concept, the constraints relating to costs, schedules, organisation, utilisation (operations, implementation,maintenance), production and disposal, as well as the estimated margins in relation to the targets.

tender.description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop and test a prototype terminal capable of DVB-S2X and RCS2 real-time switching in the return link utilising a Commercial-off-the-Shelf (COTS) modem ASIC. In a second step, the activity will develop a hub burst demodulator and scheduler, capable of using both, DVB-S2X and RCS2 frame types, allowing aflexible bandwidth share based on traffic types. End-to-end testing will include performance evaluation of the full return link comprising hub and user terminal.TargetedImprovements: Increase return link spectral efficiency up to 30% and demonstrate throughput beyond 100 Mbaud while retaining the intrinsic flexibility of MF-TDMA to retain low latency for lowthroughput applications.Description: In 2024 DVB updated the DVB-RCS2specification to include non-geostationary satellite systems. This allowed DVB-S2X constant or burst mode in the return link, allowing higher spectral efficiency and throughput. DVB-S2X and RCS2 can be mixed within the return link time plan, and a single terminalcan theoretically switch between them on the fly. This allows the increase of return link spectral efficiency up to 30%, through the implementation of S2X in the return link to carry traffic requiring large frames in a steady stream more efficiently, while retaining the ability to carry bursty, small packets more efficiently the majority of the time.This activity will be implemented in a phased approach:- In the first phase, the activity will focus to develop the software controlling the COTS modem ASIC and to develop aprototype terminal capable of DVB-S2X and RCS2 real-time switching in the return link and to test and evaluate the performance in alaboratory environment. The budget for this phase is up to 750 kEuro.- The second phase will develop a hub burst demodulator and scheduler, capable including a software or FPGA-based burst demodulator capable of switching between DVBRCS2- based MF-TDMA and DVB-S2X frames in real-time. A scheduler algorithm will be developed and tested able to accommodate the expected traffic types, with intelligent switching between frames as needed. Finally end-to-end testing will include performance evaluation of the full return link comprising hub and user terminal in a relevant environment.
tender.title: FRAME-BY-FRAME SWITCHING OF DVB-S2X AND RCS2 IN RETURN LINK (ARTES AT 3C.053) (ON DELEGATION REQUEST)

tender.description: The Agency seeks to assess the applicability and operational potential of a multi-moment, multi-fluid modelling approach for forecasting and nowcasting the Earth's magnetospheric space weather environment. While current operational systems predominantly rely on global MHD models and fully kinetic approaches remain computationally challenging for routine use, this activity aims to demonstrate whether a multi-fluid framework can provide an effective balance between physical realism and operational performance. Bidders are expected to employ real observational data for model verification, validation, calibration, and performance enhancement, investigating techniques such as data assimilation, data-driven boundary conditions, and other observation-informed methods to improve forecasting capability and scientific fidelity. The activity should include comprehensive testing against measurements and reference models, the assessment of computational performance and operational suitability, and the quantification of forecasting skill for key space weather phenomena. The work shall identify the strengths, limitations, and maturity of the approach, while establishing a clear roadmap towards a future three-dimensional global magnetospheric forecasting capability that can operate faster than real time and support advanced operational space weather services.
tender.title: HE-SWE-03B - GLOBAL MULTI-MOMENT MULTI-FLUID MODEL OF THE MAGNETOSPHERE

tender.description: Objective:The objective of this study is to develop a system concept evolving HydRON services to maritime communications and identify the technology gaps as well as the required development roadmap.Targeted Improvements:To enable maritime communications with satellite HydRON (High-throughput Optical Network) systemDescription:Maritime routes are strategic in a connected world, where economies are interdependent. 80% of the global trade depends on shipping. Current strategical routes include South China, South India, Suez Canal, Mediterranean see, trans-Atlantic and Panama Canal. Together with the current routes, the transit along the arctic seais currently becoming more attention for cargo ships but also for defence purposes. Climate change may enable the use of this route,which could mean a drastic reduction in transport costs and service time (reduction of 25-40% in distance). From a logistics perspective, cargo companies aim to monitor their goods and containers, while ports seek to receive advance information about incoming cargo to optimize and plan the unloading process.Additional to the commercial and logistic interests, the defence aspects connected to maritime communications are of special interest, especially in an arctic route, where any developed infrastructure, could enhanceresilience.Currently, maritime communications relay on low-data rate satellite communications, or the use of low-band frequencies, when the ships are located close to shore. HydRON provides space-space and space-ground connectivity, extending terrestrial networksin space and providing global coverage.The activity shall investigate user needs, requirements and system concepts for maritimecommunications (space-sea, sea-sea, sea-shore/ports), to extend the use of HydRON in maritime scenarios. Technology gaps and related technology roadmaps shall be developed, considering optical terminals and any critical technologies. The system shall consider themanagement of cloud-blockage by combining space communications with e.g. a maritime ship-to-ship free-space network or hybrid communications with RF. The space segment shall consider the coverage along the most used routes. The concept shall consider the combination of security sensitive communications with logistic traffic. Finally, the activity shall propose a demonstrator where the relevant technology as well as the operational concept can be demonstrated. The activity will also contribute to the evolution of ESTOL.

tender.description: Objective:To develop a portable modem that can be easily integrated in an existing optical ground station to make it compatible with ESTOL specificationsTargeted Improvements:Increased interoperability between existing optical ground stations and future satellite systems (e.g., HydRON).Description:There are a number of existing or planned optical ground stations (OGSs) that are currently used for scientific missions or to demonstrate quantum technologies. Those OGSs are not compliant to the ESA Specifications for Terabit/s Optical Links (ESTOL). To maximise the benefit of early Member State investments, the activity shall develop an upgrade kit" for multiple existing OGS infrastructures. An easy-to-integrate modem will facilitate the upgrade of such existing or planned OGSsand increase their interoperability with future commercial and institutional systems that will adopt ESTOL and its evolutions.Thisactivity shall develop a portable breadboard for an ESTOL-compliant modem. In the scope of the activity, it shall be assumed that thetarget existing OGSs have already been developed in terms of optical elements (e.g., aperture, adaptive optics, etc.) in order tobecompatible with ESTOL. The portable modem shall be connected to the optical part of the OGS by optical fibre, and it shall implement both transmit and receive functionalities. The modem breadboard shall come with a GUI and an interface control document to facilitate its fast and easy integration and use. tender.description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to design, manufacture and test a digital coherent and incoherent signal combining receiver that utilises multiple smalltelescopes, achieving a large effective collection area.TargetedImprovements:Reduction of system cost and complexity by using multiple small apertures to avoid the use of a larger aperture with an adaptive optics system whilemaintaining the total corresponding coupled power-in-fibre.Enabling modular system design, allowing incremental future upgrades to enhance link power budget.Description: The logical progression in optical receiver development is to use a modular receiver design with multiple apertures combined coherently and incoherently.Firstly, small aperture telescopes are significantly less affected by atmospheric disturbances and can operate with cost-effective hardware, such as tilt tracking.Secondly, advancements in large Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) and digital signal processing (DSP) blocks can significantly simplifythe optical part of the receiver and enhanced reliability, while shifting the complexity to the digital domain. Functional verification of proposed idea hasbeendemonstrated in laboratory environment by research groups.The present activity shall analyse and demonstrate via a free-space-optical experiment at minimum 10 Gbps for coherent and up to 10 Gbps for incoherentmodulation (e.g. DP-QPSK, OOK) receiver system over atmospheric turbulence conditions that are representative (or worse) of those encountered inGEO/MEO/LEO. A receiver should perform optical front-end conditioning, followed by digital coherent and incoherent multi-channel combination, and thenprovide an output toa modem.This demonstrator will feature, but not be limited to, the following critical functions: cost-efficient tilt-tracking stage, optical multi-channel front end unit withdigital coherent and incoherent combiner, electrical output to a modem.

tender.description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop and test a free-space communication link with optical key distribution (OKD) functionality.TargetedImprovements:Improvement of the key distribution rate by at least a factor of 100 with respect to QKD, alternatively, the reduction of the aperture sizes of both terminals(for the same key rate as QKD). Provision of the security assessment for OKD.Description: In the vast majority of cases, the security of communication systems is only ensured at their digital layers, leaving the lowest physical layer open toeavesdropping and interference. The primary concern in space scenarios is passive attacks, where the adversary is often able to capture an even largerportion of the signal than the legitimate receiver(s). At the same time, feasible physical layer security (PLS) solutions must meet the stringent SWaP (size,weight, and power) requirements of space missions and should be easily integrated with data transmission, even in the case of the simplest intensitymodulation/direct detection (IM/DD) links.Optical Key Distribution (OKD) is a promising solution for secure communication. It allows authenticated parties to establish a secure cryptographic key,by exploiting the high directionality of optical beams. By using optical noise, OKD is cost-effective and suitable for free-space communications, such asinter-satellite and satellite-to-ground links. The technique distributes a secure key that can be used for encryption protocols like AES, SSL/TLS, or as aone-time pad. It avoids the complexities and high costs of quantum key distribution (QKD) systems while providing adequate security for free-spacescenarios. OKD keys are quantum-safe, assuming the adversary's detection capability is limited by shot noise.The activity aims to investigate and develop a cost-effective solution for the physical layer security of optical satellite communication links, namely OpticalKey Distribution (OKD), which allows authenticated parties to establish a secure key, by monitoring the presence of an eavesdropper along the satellite to-ground line-of-sight, while avoiding the complexity and resulting significant costs of Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) systems. The activity will establishsecurity assumption for OKD and provide the security assessment of the proposed OKD system. The outcome of this work shall be evaluated by a security expert with competencies in the protection of communication links.

The result of the activity and the maturation of the ERASE concept should be in linewith the outcomes of an ESA Preliminary Requirements Review as described by the ECSS. tender.description: The objective is to develop a standardised test laboratory to evaluate the coexistence of various satellite and terrestrial systemswithin a realistic, emulated, and controlled environment.TargetedImprovements: Enable a quantified and objective assessment of mutual interferences. Reduce satcom service outage due to interference from third systems to less than 0.1%.Description: Traditional methods of interference analysis and simulation, which often rely on static models and assumptions, are insufficient to describe thereal-time interactions and variability ofsatellite and terrestrial telecommunication networks. For example, in assessing the potential interference of new NGSO systems, it is mandatory to describe the dynamic radio resourceallocation strategy of the NGSO systemunder test to assess its dynamic effects on incumbent systems such as NGSO, GSO, or terrestrial mobile networks. Moreover, current analysistools are limited to assessing the interaction between the system under test and specific victim incumbent systems, ignoring the rest of the environment, i.e. additional incumbent systemsthat may also be affected. A standardised coexistence test laboratory is essential to address these challenges. By providing a controlled environment that accurately emulates real-worldoperational scenarios, this laboratory will enable a comprehensive evaluation of spectrum coexistence. The use of standardised plug-in modules, interfaces (e.g. API, RF, IF, DIFI), anddescriptors will facilitate the modelling of various satellite and terrestrial systems and their interactions, ensuring that the assessments are both accurate and confidential. The integrationwith external RF monitoring datasets will enable a digital synthesis of the RF spectrum to establish a background digital (and protected, i.e. sandbox) environment where the tests canbe performed.This activity will develop a test laboratory comprising hardware and software components following amodular and hierarchical approach, enabling future extensibility as well as follow-up/parallel developments. The activity will first establish a development framework, including development guidelines and requirements as well as interface specifications, and thendevelop key modules sufficient to provide an initial service.

tender.description:
Objective: The objective of the activity is to define and develop a free space optical communication testbed suitable for testing a cross-atmospheric optical connectivity in the horizontal link between Tallinn and Helsinki.

Targeted Improvements: To create a terrestrial testbed capability allowing for demonstration and long-term communication testing. The testbed will provide information on the long-distance atmospheric channel and the stability of the optical links in fixed and mobile configuration. The testbed facility will support new technology developments for optical and quantum satellite communication.

Description: Most of satellite constellations developed these days include intersatellite links. However, the adaptation of cross-atmospheric links remains to be progressing slowly. One of the challenges is the limited availability of outdoor, free-space testbeds. The proposed testbed facility will enable testing over the long-distance, cross-atmospheric channel created between two stations located in Tallinn and Helsinki. 
The testbed will allow for fixed-points free-space optical connection, demonstrating and validating a continuous datalink between interoperable terminals and transceivers aligned with satellite optical communication standards. The testbed should allow to collect and analyse information on the atmospheric channel over multiple seasons. It should monitor weather conditions and investigate beam dissipation dynamics and various mitigation strategies. The spatially dynamic optical links will also be demonstrated to test and validate a free-space optical datalink between moving terminals. The testbed should foresee and facilitate testing of quantum-encrypted free-space optical communication capabilities. The preparation to demonstrate data-relay with a satellite link is planned to be included in the activity.
